feedback.gloss.battery.under: the line is at or below the battery's own voltage (%s V with an instrument); it charges only from a higher voltage
feedback.jei.info.rectifier: Set it against a battery and wire it to an MV line: while it is fed, that battery charges in about three minutes from empty instead of ten. The extra current heats the battery more and a lead-acid one gasses sooner. It draws a small current whether or not a battery is there, and does nothing alone.
feedback.jei.info.battery: A battery: cells in series that charge from any line above their voltage and give back to the line when it drops, holding their voltage nearly flat until almost empty. Build it at a bench from a stack of plates (1, 2 or 4 plates a cell in a single cell, two a cell in a stack of 3, 6 or 12 cells) and an insulating case, place it, and fill it with its electrolyte from buckets or pipes: sulfuric acid and water for lead plates, lye for nickel-iron. A powered Rectifier against it charges it in about three minutes. Overcharging boils water off and releases hydrogen, which a flame sets off; drawing too much current, running hot or sitting at a voltage above its case wears it. The cold costs capacity. A Hydrometer reads the charge.
feedback.jei.info.hydrometer: Use it on a battery to sample the acid, whose density falls as the cells discharge: it reads the state of charge to the nearest five per cent. Carry it in the instrument bag and a battery's Jade card gives the figure too.
feedback.gloss.battery.dry: the cells hold no acid yet; fill them from a bucket of sulfuric acid
feedback.gloss.battery.charging: drawing from a higher voltage on the line
feedback.gloss.battery.holding: on a line at its own voltage, neither taking nor giving
feedback.gloss.battery.soc.low: under %d%% of what the cells can hold now
feedback.gloss.battery.soc.part: %2$d%% or more of what the cells can hold now
feedback.gloss.battery.soc.nearly: %3$d%% or more of what the cells can hold now
feedback.gloss.battery.soc.full: as full as the cells go
feedback.gloss.battery.weeping: overcharged: it is boiling water into hydrogen. A flame near it is dangerous
feedback.gloss.battery.low_water: the plates are exposed and the cells hold less; top the water up
modular.feedback.role.plates.tip: The stack of plates. Its material sets the volts of a cell, how much charge a plate holds and how it fares in the cold; its size sets how many cells.
modular.feedback.role.case.tip: What holds the stack. Its material sets the highest voltage the battery can take without wearing.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.light_cell: A single plate for the cell: half the charge of the standard pair, 1 cell.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.heavy_cell: Four plates of stock for one cell: twice the charge of the standard pair, 1 cell.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.three_cell: Like a pair of plates, but 6 plates of stock: 3 cells in series, 3 times the volts.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.six_cell: Like a pair of plates, but 12 plates of stock: 6 cells in series, 6 times the volts.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.twelve_cel: Like a pair of plates, but 24 plates of stock: 12 cells in series, 12 times the volts.
modular.feedback.desc.part.battery_plate: Plates of a metal that can be charged and discharged, laid in a stack. Two plates make a cell, so a pair is one cell, six plates three, twelve plates six and twenty-four twelve. Cells in series add their volts but not their capacity. A metal whose plates do not take a charge makes a stack that holds none.
feedback.battery.dry: No acid: the cells are dry
tooltip.feedback.battery.dry: Dry: fill the cells with acid once placed
modular.feedback.desc.part.machine_frame: The frame the shaft's torque is carried through, in plate. Its size sets the most torque the machine carries (2, 16 or 64 Su), how much heat it holds and how large a wall it sheds heat through.
modular.feedback.desc.part.machine_windi: The coil of wire. Its turns set the volts per RPM, and so the speed a motor runs at per volt and the volts a generator makes per RPM; its wire sets the current it carries, and the loss it makes as heat.
modular.feedback.desc.part.machine_housi: The shell that sheds the machine's heat to the air, in plate. A metal that conducts heat well sheds more; a cooling addon fitted to it (plate fins, or pipe for a water jacket) sheds more.
modular.feedback.role.frame.tip: Carries the torque. Its size sets the most the machine can carry, and its heat capacity.
modular.feedback.role.machine_winding.ti: The coil. Its material must conduct: its current rating sets the amps; its turns set the volts per RPM.
modular.feedback.role.housing.tip: Sheds the machine's heat to the air. Its material's heat conduction sets how fast.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.small: Carries 2 Su of torque at most.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.medium: 4 plates of stock: carries 16 Su of torque at most.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.large: 8 plates of stock: carries 64 Su of torque at most.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.coarse: A single wire: few turns, few volts per RPM.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.fine: 2 wires of stock: four times the volts per RPM of coarse.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.dense: 4 wires of stock: sixteen times the volts per RPM of coarse, 360 V at a gas turbine's speed.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.heavy_dens: 8 wires of stock: sixty-four times the volts per RPM of coarse.
tooltip.feedback.dynamotor.jacket: Water jacket: fill it with water once placed
feedback.jei.info.dynamotor: Turns rotation into electricity and back: a frame, a winding, a core and a housing built at a bench. Place it against the end of a shaft and run cable from any other face. Sneak-right-click with an empty hand to switch it between generator and motor. The winding's turns set the volts per RPM, its wire the current; a bigger frame carries more torque. It heats in use and sheds the heat through its housing; a cooling addon of plate (fins) sheds more, and one of pipe is a water jacket that takes water from a bucket to shed twice as fast. Overdrawing it wears it, but never stops it.

feedback.jei.info.joint_link: Ties two bodies at a joint. Click a joint voxel that has nothing in front of it, then a voxel of the other body within a block and a half of its face: that body is held to the joint, as a body made from the blocks in front of it would be, but nothing is made and nothing is used up. Click the joint voxel with an empty hand to let it go. A chain closed this way is a loop; the Lift reports it, and the physics does what it can with it.

message.feedback.link.linked: Linked: the other body is held to the joint
message.feedback.link.other_world: The world is not a body to hold: pick a voxel of a lifted body
message.feedback.link.same_body: That is the joint's own body
message.feedback.link.too_far: Too far from the joint: within a block and a half
message.feedback.differential.mode.0: Open: the axle that resists less turns faster
message.feedback.differential.mode.1: Limited slip: the axles may differ by only a little
feedback.jei.info.differential: One shaft in, two axles out. The speed is shared by what each axle resists: open, the axle with less grip spins and the other stands; limited slip, they may differ by only a little; locked, a solid axle. Sneak-click to change. Place it on a shaft, as a block or as a micro-block; the axles go out across the way you look.
message.feedback.joint.repaired: Fitted a new bearing: the joint and its brake pad are as built
feedback.jei.info.tire_rubber: Synthetic rubber pressed into a block. Place it as micro-blocks round a Rotary Bearing and the turned part is a wheel with a softer, grippier tread than black wool.
feedback.jei.info.micro_wedge: A four-step ramp. Place it as a micro-block and it is a ramp a quarter of a block long, falling away from you; click the top half of a face to hang it from above. What you see is what collides. Set the Micro Core to Wedge mode and any whole block in your other hand goes in as a ramp of itself.
feedback.jei.info.ball_joint: A micro-block joint. Put it in a micro cell with its front towards what should swing, then use it with an empty hand: everything joined to its front face becomes a body that swings about the joint inside a cone. Sneak-use before assembling to choose a narrow, stock or wide cone.
feedback.jei.info.locked_joint: A micro-block joint that holds two bodies as one rigid piece, so a part can be split off and put back later. Use it with an empty hand to assemble or put back.
feedback.jei.info.slider_joint: A micro-block joint that lets a body slide along its front axis against a spring: a suspension. Sneak-use before assembling to choose a soft, stock or stiff spring.
feedback.jei.info.piston_joint: A micro-block joint that slides a body along its front axis to a level a controller card sets. It holds the position against a load and wears only if forced past it.

feedback.jei.info.rolling_mill: Rolls an ingot into a plate. A brittle stock (a mineral, crystal, ceramic or glass ingot or gem) does not flatten: the rolls grind it to dust, which reacts and melts faster than the lump. A ductile metal cannot be ground; its dust comes from a melt shattered in water in an atomising mold. Lay a second plate on a plate in the mill and roll it to clad the first with a skin of the second's metal: both plates must be hot enough to bond, and a skin rolled near its melting point comes out burnt. Hand a clad plate to a bench as the wearing part and the tool keeps the coat.

skill.feedback.move.concealed_carry.desc: Creatures notice you from nearer while you hold a weapon that is quiet and light (stealth 60% or more, the Suits: quiet word), in proportion to how quiet it is. A held item above the burn line glows and is seen: no help from it.
skill.feedback.move.hush_the_kill.desc: A blow that kills an unaware creature, from a weapon with half its stealth or more, makes no vibration for sculk to hear.
skill.feedback.move.dull_edge.desc: A weapon with a soft, dull edge (hardness under 2.5) clanks less: its blows carry a fifth nearer to sculk sensors and wardens.
skill.feedback.move.muffled_report.desc: A gun whose report is under one and a half times the quiet band sends the quietest gunshot vibration, so a suppressed or low-report gun passes sculk unheard further out.
skill.feedback.move.clawhold.desc: With claws on your hands, a wall run lasts twice as long along wood, dirt or leaves, which claws bite into. Stone and glass give them nothing to hold.
skill.feedback.move.opening_cut.desc: Claws on an unaware or back-turned creature open a bleed twice as deep.
skill.feedback.move.gouge.desc: A claw hit on a creature already bleeding stacks the bleed, up to three, and leaves it in a new kind of disorder (bleeding).
skill.feedback.move.tear_straps.desc: Claw hits rake the target's worn armour, wearing each piece, and wear the claws themselves a point a hit (never the last).
skill.feedback.move.burning_ground.desc: Kindle lays its fire on any floor, not only on what burns, and keeps relighting it for as long as the item's heat lasts. The item cools by every spot lit.
skill.feedback.move.overwatch.desc: Cast: hold a loaded gun on a lane for five seconds. Every living thing that crosses the aim cone within twenty blocks is pinned as by Pin down, with no shot fired. Each one caught costs 6 stamina; the watch ends if you move off the spot or put the gun away. Costs 25 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.suppressing_fire.des: Held cast: hold the key and the gun fires a round every few ticks, each laid to one side or the other of your aim and sweeping back and forth across a cone that follows where you look, never on a target. Pin down slows whatever a round passes close to. Every round spends ammo and heats the barrel, and it ends on an empty gun, an empty bar or letting go. Costs 20 stamina, then 6 a second while held.
skill.feedback.move.plate_up.desc: Brace holds with your worn armour's toughness as well as its mass: each point adds to what holds a blow.
skill.feedback.move.phalanx.desc: Allies standing behind you within three blocks are covered by Shield wall too.
skill.feedback.move.pavise.desc: Cast, crouched behind a shield: for four seconds every arrow, bolt and bullet that comes at you from the front is stopped, not turned. The shield wears for the force it stops; you cannot leave the spot. Costs 25 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.lee_side.desc: Crouched with a full block against you, a tether pulls you half as hard and knockback is halved.
skill.feedback.move.called_draw.desc: Called shot works with a bow or crossbow: call the creature under your crosshair and the next arrow you loose flies at where it will be when it arrives.
skill.feedback.move.held_draw.desc: Holding a full draw for a second steadies the arrow: it leaves exactly down your look. Holding drains stamina, and past five seconds your hands shake and the steadiness is lost.
skill.feedback.move.tipping_point.desc: A blow from a precise weapon (precision 50% or more, the Suits: precise word) that lands at the tip of the reach goes past a quarter of the target's armour and does not knock it back.
skill.feedback.move.thread_the_gap.desc: A precise weapon's Soft spot blow also staggers the target, longer the more precise the weapon.
modular.feedback.desc.part.charge_casing: The shell round a charge. Its shape decides whether it holds the blast in or breaks into fragments.
modular.feedback.desc.part.charge_primer: A small starter that sets the whole filler going.
modular.feedback.role.primer.tip: Optional. A booster makes the filler burn through for a harder blast and less fire; a flash primer makes the charge throw fire.
modular.feedback.role.payload.tip: Optional. Hard bits packed round the filler become shrapnel; a luminous powder makes a flash that blinds.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.tight_casi: Thick and unscored: holds the gas in, a harder blast, few fragments.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.scored_cas: Cut to break up: far more fragments, a softer blast.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.booster_pr: Burns the filler through: a harder blast, less fire.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.flash_prim: Throws the unburnt filler as fire.
modular.feedback.desc.part.charge_fuse: A wick or a striker that sets a charge off. A wick burns for a time; a striker goes off on a blow.
modular.feedback.role.fuse.tip: How the charge is set off: a wick burns short, standard or long, or a striker goes off on the first hard hit. A charge with no fuse part burns the standard wick.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.short_fuse: A short wick: about 1.5 seconds from lighting to blast.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.delay_fuse: A standard wick: about 3 seconds from lighting to blast.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.long_fuse: A long wick: about 6 seconds from lighting to blast.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.impact_fus: A striker: a thrown charge goes off on the first thing it hits. A placed charge is lit by hand on the standard wick.
message.feedback.press.missing: Needs a case and a bullet.
message.feedback.press.too_much: A case takes at most %s charge.
message.feedback.gun.chain_fire: A pointed bullet set off the round ahead of it in the tube!
gun.feedback.spent: Spent: the chamber has let go

modular.feedback.desc.variant.slicer: Long and thin: it follows the stroke across tough fiber, but skids on fat.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.turner: A plain blade: turns one piece.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.wide_turne: A broad blade: turns two pieces side by side with one click.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.slotted_tu: Slots in the blade let juice run off: each piece loses a tenth of its moisture as it is turned.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.peen: A lean head with its weight in the peen: lighter, but lands a blow a fifth sharper for its weight.

modular.feedback.role.bearing.tip: Optional. Sets how much torque the rotor carries and how much friction heat it makes. A machine with none runs on its frame's own bore.

modular.feedback.desc.variant.ball_beari: Balls in a race: runs cool and carries more torque.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.roller_bea: Rollers in a race: carries the most torque, with a little friction.
modular.feedback.desc.part.tool_pommel: A weight on the end of the handle, behind the hand.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.knob: A small cap on the handle's end.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.ball: A heavier ball behind the hand: the head comes round a little faster.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.flat_ring: A plain flat ring: a mild seal.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.cup_seal: A cupped seal that grips the case: much less kick, little else.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.double_rin: Two rings: a tighter group, less kick cut.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.dot_reticl: A dot that shows in the dark (light level 7 or less).
modular.feedback.desc.variant.ring_retic: A wide ring that shows in dim light (11 or less) but tightens the group less.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.cross_reti: A fine cross that shows only in deep dark (4 or less) and tightens the group most.

feedback.jei.info.cryocooler: A cold head on a wire (MV, 6 A). It chills the face it points at, the way it was placed, far under room temperature; a vessel against that face (a Reactor) settles a little short of the head's temperature, and a head with no power holds nothing. Right-click with an empty hand to cycle its stage: deep (about -194 Tu on the vessel), middle (about -190) or shallow (about -185). Compressed air liquefies only at the deep stage; warming that liquid air to the middle stage boils nitrogen off ahead of the oxygen; the shallow stage then boils argon off ahead of the oxygen. Too warm a stage does not separate: the cold liquid simply boils back to air.
feedback.stockpot.thin: There is nothing in it worth ladling.

feedback.electrolytic_cell.anode: Hung as the anode, to dissolve

feedback.coherer.stuck: Coherer tapped: grains sintered, still welded

feedback.readout.xp_run: Run at level %s, %s points; moving %s, leaking %s
feedback.jei.info.large_boiler: Ten Boilers in one block: ten times the water, steam and steam a tick, and it stands on ten times the fire, so it wants a hotter, bigger firebox than one Boiler does. It makes the 100 mB of steam a tick a Steam Turbine drinks. It can burst like a Boiler if its line is shut under a real fire. Built from a shell part at a Smithing Table from a blueprint (Chemical Treatise I): the shell's wall, shape and metal set the pressure it risks letting go at, and the valve and seams follow it. Optional hoop bands raise the line.
feedback.debug.heat_probe.total: Heat reaching this block: %1$s Tu (ambient %2$s Tu)
feedback.debug.heat_probe.source: from %2$s on the %1$s side: fire %3$s Tu, reach %4$s%% (it faces %5$s)
screen.feedback.creative.gas: Gas (0 = bucket fluid, else nth gas)
feedback.data_connector.wire: A link that long needs %s wire in your inventory.
feedback.data_connector.range: No wire reaches that far (%s blocks).
feedback.data_connector.mode.clear: cut every link on a node
feedback.readout.wire.bare: Bare: shocks, and arcs to a bare wire an air block away
feedback.tooltip.cable.insulated: Insulated to %s; a higher voltage burns it off
feedback.tooltip.cable.bare: Bare: shocks, and arcs to a bare wire an air block away
feedback.jei.cable.gauge_note: Fine wire gives thin cable, wire standard, four wires in a square heavy, and a plate a bus bar
feedback.jei.cable.insulate: Three of an insulating material in a row below coat the cable
feedback.gloss.jar.charging: drawing current from its line; anything else on the line gets less
feedback.gloss.jar.holding: charged or full and drawing nothing
feedback.gloss.jar.discharging: giving its charge back as a source
tooltip.feedback.copper_bucket.empty: Empty. Use on a fluid source to fill it.
tooltip.feedback.jar_baton.empty: Empty. Use on a charged Leyden jar to draw its charge.
feedback.jei.tool_table_tool.dish: Made at the Prep Table: pick this dish there, then put in a container and foods. The parts decide what is made, and a seasoning is poured on at the end.
feedback.jei.tool_table_tool.slots: Six slots; the parts decide what is made, and they may sit in any slot.
feedback.jei.tool_table_part.note: Choose the shape at the table and put the stock in its cells. Steel and the like must be hot.
feedback.jei.tool_table_part.forged: Forged: choose it at the table, put in the stock, and play the pattern. Steel and the like must be hot.
feedback.jei.modular.tip: Tip: a Tip part (a gem, shard or nugget shaped at a bench, harder than the body) in a spare slot, or added to a finished tool in the tool slot. Bites like the tip, holds like the body.
feedback.jei.modular.binding: Binding: a Binding part (string, leather or wire shaped at a bench) in a spare slot, or added to a finished tool. A stronger binding holds a heavier head.
feedback.jei.modular.studs: Studs: gems set in the plate, each covering a tenth. Hardness without a brittle plate.
feedback.jei.modular.grind: Edge: shift-use a grindstone to change it, at a little durability.
feedback.jei.modular.coat: Plate it in an electrolytic cell for a coat: corrosion resistance, and a harder skin on armor.
tooltip.feedback.mold.nothing: This mold can make nothing of it
tooltip.feedback.mold.set: Set: use it to turn it out
feedback.jei.reaction.bed: a bed of the catalyst in the slot
feedback.jei.material.kind.tip: What sort of stuff this is. Hover the value to see why it matters.
feedback.jei.material.hardness.tip: How hard it is to cut or deform. Each blow does less work on harder material.
feedback.jei.material.density.tip: Mass per volume. Denser things weigh more and sink in lighter fluids.
feedback.jei.material.melting_point.tip: The temperature where it turns liquid.
feedback.jei.material.boiling_point.tip: The temperature where it turns to vapor.
feedback.jei.material.anneal.tip: Heat it past this and it softens, so it can be worked and relieved of stress.
feedback.jei.material.service.tip: The hottest it can sit for long without weakening.
feedback.jei.material.oxidation.tip: Above this temperature air starts to burn, char or rust it.
feedback.jei.material.thermal_conductivi: How fast heat moves through it. High means it warms and cools quickly.
feedback.jei.material.cooling_rate.tip: How quickly it loses heat to the air around it.
feedback.jei.material.toughness.tip: How much punishment it takes before it breaks.
feedback.jei.material.ductility.tip: How far it can be bent or drawn before it cracks.
feedback.jei.material.yield.tip: How much load it takes before it stays bent.
feedback.jei.material.friction.tip: How much it grips against other surfaces.
feedback.jei.material.abrasiveness.tip: How much it wears down whatever rubs on it.
feedback.jei.material.hardenable.tip: Heating then quenching it makes it much harder.
feedback.jei.material.electrical_conduct: How easily current flows through it.
feedback.jei.material.corrosion.tip: How well it holds up against rust and decay. Higher is better.
feedback.jei.material.flame.tip: How hot it burns when used as fuel.
feedback.jei.material.flash_point.tip: The temperature where it gives off vapor that can catch fire.
feedback.jei.material.burn_ticks.tip: How long it burns as fuel, in ticks (20 ticks is a second).
feedback.jei.material.ignition.tip: The temperature where it ignites as a propellant.
How strongly it speeds up a reaction without being used up.
feedback.jei.material.oxygen_fraction.ti: The share of this gas that is oxygen a lung can use.
feedback.jei.material.xp_top_level.tip: The highest level an XP container of this material can stand at.
feedback.jei.material.xp_capacitance.tip: Points of XP one cell of this material holds.
feedback.jei.material.xp_conductance.tip: Points a tick an XP wire of this material moves for each level of difference.
feedback.jei.material.xp_leak.tip: The share of what moves through the wire that escapes as XP orbs.
feedback.jei.material.moisture.tip: How wet it is. Wet food spoils faster and cooks slower.
feedback.jei.material.fat.tip: How much fat it has. It makes a dish richer and heavier.
feedback.jei.material.fibre.tip: How much fiber it has. It makes a dish denser.
feedback.jei.material.pathogen.tip: How many germs raw it carries. Cooking clears it.
feedback.jei.material.toxin.tip: How much poison it holds. Cooking may not remove it.
feedback.jei.material.qu_note: A figure in Qu is an amount per item: one Qu is the amount of metal in a nugget.
feedback.jei.material.char.tip: The temperature where it burns instead of cooking.
feedback.jei.material.shelf.tip: How much slower it spoils than ordinary food.
feedback.jei.compound.sugar.tip: Eaten, gives a burst of speed. A slowdown follows when it wears off.
feedback.jei.compound.stimulant.tip: Eaten, gives haste. Mining fatigue follows when it wears off.
feedback.jei.compound.protein.tip: Eaten, gives strength for a while.
feedback.jei.compound.mineral.tip: Eaten, gives damage resistance for a while.
feedback.jei.compound.vitamin.tip: Eaten, gives night vision for a while.
feedback.jei.kind.metal.tip: Hammered, cast and rolled into plates, rods and wire. Conducts heat and electricity.
feedback.jei.kind.mineral.tip: Stone, rock and mineral stuff. Hard and heavy, cut or ground, not hammered.
feedback.jei.kind.crystal.tip: Gems and ordered solids. Brittle and clear, cut and ground.
feedback.jei.kind.ceramic.tip: Fired clay. Heat-proof and hard, but it shatters.
feedback.jei.kind.glass.tip: Melted and blown or cast. Clear and brittle.
feedback.jei.kind.granular.tip: Sand, dust and powder. It pours and packs, and is shaped by moulds.
feedback.jei.kind.organic.tip: Wood, bone and plant matter. Light and easy to cut, and it burns.
feedback.jei.kind.grain.tip: Seeds of grasses and legumes. Dry, keeps long, and is milled or boiled.
feedback.jei.kind.vegetable.tip: Roots, leaves and stems. Wet and fibrous, cooked or eaten raw, and spoils.
feedback.jei.kind.fruit.tip: Sweet, juicy plant flesh. Eaten as it is, and spoils fast.
feedback.jei.kind.fungus.tip: Mushrooms. Wet and earthy, cooked or dried.
feedback.jei.kind.flower.tip: Petals and blooms. Light and scented, wilts quickly, and steeps well.
feedback.jei.kind.herb.tip: Leaves, ferns and green stems. Fragrant, dries well, and steeps well.
feedback.jei.kind.animal.tip: Flesh and eggs. Rich in protein, and spoils unless cooked or cured.
feedback.jei.kind.seafood.tip: Fish. Wet and delicate, and spoils fastest of all.
feedback.jei.kind.dough.tip: Flour worked into a mass, then baked or boiled. Kneaded, rolled and cut.
feedback.jei.kind.dish.tip: Cooked and combined foods, served from a pot or bowl.
feedback.jei.kind.sculk.tip: A living-looking mass that can be rolled into plates.
feedback.jei.kind.fluid.tip: Poured and piped, never cut. It is stored in tanks and moved by pumps.
feedback.jei.kind.polymer.tip: Plastics and rubbers. Moulded and cast like a metal, but light and insulating.
feedback.jei.perk.fire_aspect.tip: Sets what it hits on fire. A bare hand gets burned.
feedback.jei.perk.echo.tip: A struck target is outlined and heard by sculk.
feedback.jei.perk.featherlight.tip: Swings as if it were lighter.
feedback.jei.perk.bounce.tip: A struck target is thrown up.
feedback.jei.perk.radiant.tip: A struck target withers and glows.
feedback.jei.perk.siphon.tip: Kills give a little extra experience.
feedback.jei.perk.blink.tip: A kill steps you into its place.
message.feedback.lift.lifted: Lifted. Use to raise, sneak-use to lower, sneak-use at the bottom to put it back as blocks, break the lift to drop it.
message.feedback.lift.lowered: Back in the world as blocks.
message.feedback.lift.blocked: Something is in the way of putting it back as blocks.
message.feedback.lift.too_big: Too big -- is it touching something besides the lift?
message.feedback.lift.on_vehicle: This lift is part of a vehicle -- it can't lift.
message.feedback.lift.loops: %s closed joint loops: they will be stiff and may jitter.
message.feedback.lift.joined: Two vehicles are joined to this one at a joint -- put the joint back to carry them apart.
message.feedback.lift.no_room: No room to put it down here.
tooltip.feedback.grapple.multi: Second hook: two lines at once
feedback.jei.info.grapple_winch: A drum on a crank in a frame. Craft it with a grapple in the crafting grid to fit it: the reel runs faster.
tooltip.feedback.grapple.barb: Barbed head: reels in lighter creatures
feedback.jei.info.grapple: A hook on a line. Use throws it; it bites a block or a creature. On a block (or a creature heavier than you) you swing from it as a pendulum; hold use to winch the line in, sneak to let go, and the speed you carry when you let go is thrown on. Fittings, each made with the grapple in the crafting grid: 4 string for a longer line, a grapple winch for a faster reel, 2 wrought iron rods for a barbed head that reels lighter creatures to you, 3 wrought iron plates for a second hook head: using the grapple again with a line out throws a second line, and both lines hold you. A line over its load strains and parts.
