tooltip.feedback.attuned.draw_round: Bends the round toward heavy armour (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.draw_round: bends the fired round toward the nearest heavily armoured living thing ahead, keeping its speed. Goes dead when the barrel is hotter than its Curie point.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.fling_round: Bends the round away from heavy armour (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.fling_roun: bends the fired round away from heavily armoured living things ahead, keeping its speed. Goes dead when the barrel is hotter than its Curie point.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.wet_round: Round keeps its speed under water (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.wet_round: lets the fired round keep its speed through water.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.dry_round: loses a share of the round's damage on a target that is not in water.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.charged_round: Arcs a share of each hit (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.charged_ro: arcs a share of each hit to the nearest other living thing within a few blocks that is wet or in heavy armour, and calls lightning on a sky-exposed target in a thunderstorm.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.grounded_r: sheds charge into the ground: the target takes a share less damage.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.channel: draws lightning to the holder in a thunderstorm under open sky, and calls a bolt on everything it hits, or on the ground a slam strikes.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.draw: Draws the drops of what you kill to you (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.draw: sends the drops of whatever the blow kills flying to the wielder. Goes dead when the part is hotter than its Curie point.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.fling: Throws the drops of what you kill away (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.fling: throws the drops of whatever the blow kills away from the wielder. Goes dead when the part is hotter than its Curie point.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.worn_draw: while worn, loose items nearby drift toward you. Goes dead when the part is hotter than its Curie point.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.worn_fling: while worn, arrows and tridents with metal in them are turned aside before they hit you. Goes dead when the part is hotter than its Curie point.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.ring: a landed blow rings, so sculk and nearby hostile mobs notice it from further.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.hush: A landed blow makes no sound (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.hush: the blow and the hurt it causes make no vibration for sculk to feel.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.worn_ring: while worn, your steps and the hits you take ring, so sculk and nearby hostile mobs notice you.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.worn_hush: Worn: steps and hits are silent (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.worn_hush: while worn, your steps and the hits you take make no vibration for sculk to feel.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.stick: A landed blow sticks and slows (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.stick: a landed blow sticks to the target and slows it, longer the grippier the material.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.slick: A landed blow knocks the target sliding (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.slick: a landed blow knocks the target further along, more the slipperier the material.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.worn_grip: on a boot, stops a slide on slippery ground when you are not pushing, more the grippier the material.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.worn_slick: on a boot, lets you skate faster on any ground but stops poorly.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.glow: while held, carries a light that moves with you.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.dim: Held: hides you in the dark (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.dim: while held, hostile mobs beyond a short range do not take you up as a target while you stand in low light.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.worn_glow: while worn, carries a light that moves with you.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.worn_dim: Worn: hides you in the dark (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.worn_dim: while worn, hostile mobs beyond a short range do not take you up as a target while you stand in low light.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.worn_lure: while worn, draws passive animals nearby toward you, no item in hand needed.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.worn_scare: Worn: scatters animals and weak monsters (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.worn_scare: while worn, animals and weak hostile mobs nearby keep their distance from you.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.worn_grow: Worn on boots: walking grows crops and grass (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.worn_grow: on boots, walking grows crops and spreads grass underfoot every few blocks.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.worn_reap: Worn on boots: walking reaps ripe crops (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.worn_reap: on boots, walking over ripe crops harvests and replants them every few blocks.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.worn_reserve: Worn: sprinting and fighting cost less hunger (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.worn_reser: cuts the hunger you burn from sprinting and fighting.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.worn_famine: Worn: whoever hits you loses hunger (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.worn_famin: whoever hits you loses food if a player, or is weakened if a mob.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.worn_sprint: Worn on legs or boots: the longer you run straight, the faster (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.worn_sprin: on legs or boots, the longer you run in a straight line the faster you go, to a cap; stopping or a sharp turn resets it.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.worn_stance: Worn: standing still builds damage reduction (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.worn_stanc: the longer you stand still the less damage you take, to a cap; moving resets it.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.momentum: Hits harder after a straight sprint (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.momentum: hits harder and knocks further the longer you ran in a straight line before the blow; a spear jab after a sprint is the best hit.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.brace: hits harder the longer you have stood still; moving breaks it.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.pack: Hits harder for each ally near (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.pack: hits harder for each ally within a few blocks: same team, same tamed owner, or a golem.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.pack_guard: Takes less from a hit for each ally near (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.pack_guard: turns away more of a hit for each ally within a few blocks.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.lone: Hits harder with no ally near (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.lone: hits harder when no ally is within a few blocks.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.lone_guard: Takes less from a hit with no ally near (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.lone_guard: turns away more of a hit when no ally is within a few blocks.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.mark: marks the target, which glows; the next blow on it, from anyone, does extra.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.taunt: Draws hostile mobs onto the wearer (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.taunt: marks its wearer, so hostile mobs nearby turn on them. Brittle.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.echo_blow: Repeats each blow a beat later (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.echo_blow: repeats each blow on the same target a beat later, at a share of its damage.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.echo_wear: wears the part extra on every hit you take. The damage is unchanged.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.lag_blow: makes each swing land a few seconds after it is struck.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.lag_hit: puts off a share of each hit you take and delivers it over the next few seconds.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.gamble: flips a coin on each blow: it lands for double damage, or heals the target instead.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.gamble_war: flips a coin on each hit you take: it does double damage, or none at all.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.feed: restores food and saturation on a kill, and costs a little hunger on every blow.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.drain: takes food from a player it hits, and weakens a mob.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.grudge: Damage you take fills the charge bar (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.grudge: damage the wearer takes is stored in the charge bar of the Charge tool in hand, to be spent by the next release.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.calm: Damage you take drains the charge bar (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.calm: damage the wearer takes bleeds stored charge from the Charge tool in hand.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.grow: Swing grows crops and grass nearby (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.grow: a swing at the ground grows crops and spreads grass in a small area, then cools down.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.reap: a swing at the ground harvests and replants ripe crops in a small area, then cools down.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.lure: while held, draws passive animals nearby toward you.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.scare: while held, animals and weak hostile mobs nearby flee from you.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.pulse: Strikes a Leyden jar to charge it by hand (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.pulse: strikes charge a Leyden jar a little by hand; a blow on anything else is lost.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.sense: Tells you how hard each blow landed (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.sense: tells you in words how hard each landed blow was; it controls nothing.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.cycle_gaug: tells you in words how hard each shot landed, and in a figure if you carry an instrument; it controls nothing.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.vent_hot: puts more heat into the barrel with every shot, so it reaches the hot bands sooner.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.vent_cold: lets the barrel shed heat faster between shots.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.run_gun: Shots hit harder after a run (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.run_gun: shots fired on the run hit harder the longer you ran in a straight line.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.brace_gun: tightens the spread of a shot after standing still a moment.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.reserve: holds experience points. Sneak-use in the air passes experience from whoever stands at the higher level to whoever stands at the lower, sneak-use on a creative experience source fills it up to the source's level; mending draws on it before you.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.build: Each blow builds charge, released on a sneak-use (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.build: each blow builds charge; sneak-use arms a release that spends it all in the next blow (or, on a head that also draws lightning, spends some to call a bolt in any weather). Too much charge arcs through the wielder unless the handle insulates.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.capacitor: Widens the charge bar of the tool in hand (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.capacitor: while worn, widens the charge bar of a Charge tool in hand: more charge held before it arcs.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.bleed: Sheds charge each blow, a ground strap (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bleed: sheds stored charge each blow, and the wielder is never arced.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.point_magn: a needle in the action bar leans toward the nearest block of iron-bearing rock. It dies when the part is heated past its Curie point.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.away_magne: a needle in the action bar leans away from the nearest block of iron-bearing rock. It dies when the part is heated past its Curie point.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.point_dens: a needle in the action bar leans toward the nearest block of the heavy seams.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.away_dense: Needle away from the heavy seams (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.away_dense: a needle in the action bar leans away from the nearest block of the heavy seams.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.point_conductiv: Needle toward metals that carry current (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.point_cond: a needle in the action bar leans toward the nearest block of metals that carry current.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.away_conductive: Needle away from metals that carry current (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.away_condu: a needle in the action bar leans away from the nearest block of metals that carry current.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.point_flam: a needle in the action bar leans toward the nearest block of what will burn.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.away_flammable: Needle away from what will burn (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.away_flamm: a needle in the action bar leans away from the nearest block of what will burn.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.worn_point: when nothing held reads, a needle in the action bar leans toward the nearest block of iron-bearing rock. It dies when the part is heated past its Curie point.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.worn_away_magne: Worn needle away from iron-bearing rock (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.worn_away_: when nothing held reads, a needle in the action bar leans away from the nearest block of iron-bearing rock. It dies when the part is heated past its Curie point.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.worn_point_dens: Worn needle toward the heavy seams (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.worn_point: when nothing held reads, a needle in the action bar leans toward the nearest block of the heavy seams.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.worn_away_dense: Worn needle away from the heavy seams (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.worn_away_: when nothing held reads, a needle in the action bar leans away from the nearest block of the heavy seams.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.worn_point_cond: Worn needle toward metals that carry current (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.worn_point: when nothing held reads, a needle in the action bar leans toward the nearest block of metals that carry current.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.worn_away_condu: Worn needle away from metals that carry current (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.worn_away_: when nothing held reads, a needle in the action bar leans away from the nearest block of metals that carry current.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.worn_point_flam: Worn needle toward what will burn (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.worn_point: when nothing held reads, a needle in the action bar leans toward the nearest block of what will burn.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.worn_away_flamm: Worn needle away from what will burn (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.worn_away_: when nothing held reads, a needle in the action bar leans away from the nearest block of what will burn.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.arc: A blow it takes arcs onto the attacker (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.arc: a blow it takes arcs onto whatever struck it, harder for a harder hit; an insulating plate arcs nothing.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.soak: turns away some of the wear each use causes.
feedback.reservoir.full: The reservoir is full, or you have none to give.
feedback.charge.armed: Charge armed: the next blow releases it.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.insulate: Turns fire away from the wearer (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.insulate: turns fire damage away from the wearer, better the poorer a conductor the material is.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.mend: repairs itself while held or worn, paid for in your experience points; it drains the experience you wanted to keep.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.fortune: gets more out of what it breaks or kills.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.intact: breaks blocks out whole, not into their loot.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.recall: a magnetic head pulls the weapon back to the thrower after it lands.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.anchor: a thrown weapon that strikes plants the target, which cannot move for a short time.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.brass_retu: a magnetic receiver, if not heated past its Curie point, sometimes puts the spent round back in the magazine.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.anchor_rou: a bullet that hits plants the target, which is slowed to a standstill for a short time.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.field_roun: a bullet landing on a growing crop bone-meals it.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.reap_round: a bullet landing on a ripe crop harvests it.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.rewind: sneak-use snaps the wearer back to where they stood a few seconds ago, with a long cooldown and a little wear; it refuses if the spot is blocked.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.coil: on legs or boots, holding sneak compresses the wearer and a jump releases a launch scaled by the hold, with a little wear per release.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.scavenge: worn, it adds a share to every experience orb picked up, up to a cap.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.store: stores more draw energy, so the shot leaves faster at the same draw time.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.release: lets go sooner, so the draw or load takes less time.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.seal: Seals against water, breath lasts longer (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.seal: seals out water, so breath lasts longer.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.stride: cuts the drag of wading through water.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.clamp: Cannot be thrown from the hand (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.clamp: clamps to the hand, so the tool cannot be dropped.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.freeze: Stacks freezing on what it strikes (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.freeze: stacks freezing on what it strikes, slowing it and then hurting it.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.walker: cools lava under the wearer's feet to obsidian, which runs again soon after. Boots only.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.douse: Puts out fires, and hurts what water hurts (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.douse: puts out what it strikes and the fires it is used beside, and hurts blazes and anything else water hurts.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.slip: May leave the hand when it strikes (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.slip: may slip from your hand when you strike, but the loose handle gives under force.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.kickback: Throws you and what you hit apart when it fires (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.kickback: recoils hard when it fires: you are thrown back along the shot and the target is thrown the other way.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.kin_calm: Calms what it strikes among the undead, and they hit harder for it (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.kin_calm: makes the undead it strikes lose interest in you for a while, but they hit harder while it lasts.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.kin_hide: The undead notice you from less far, and hit harder (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.kin_hide: makes the undead notice the wearer from less far away, but they hit harder when they do.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.pad: Spreads the blow: less damage, a stagger (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.pad: turns part of the damage into a stagger, slowing and weakening what it strikes.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.pull: Draws what it strikes toward you (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.pull: draws what it strikes in toward the wielder.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.drag: Draws you and what you hit together when it fires (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.drag: pulls the shooter after the shot and the target back toward them when it fires.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.tithe: Pays experience for kills, and wears for it (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.tithe: pays out experience for what it kills and wears a little for each kill.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.limber: frees the legs, so crouching is less slow.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.shed: sheds the damage and fire of lightning.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.deflect: turns projectiles aside, the harder the better.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.bane: Cuts deeper into the undead and arthropods (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bane: cuts deeper into the undead and arthropods.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.bane_ward: Blunts blows from the undead and arthropods (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.bane_ward: blunts blows from the undead and arthropods.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.shove: throws back what it strikes, heavy things less.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.recoil: kicks the wielder back when they strike.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.reflect: Returns a share of the blow to the attacker (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.reflect: returns a share of each blow to whoever struck the wearer.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.burn_wield: burns the hand that holds it.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.desc.ignite_att: sets whoever strikes the wearer alight.
tooltip.feedback.attuned.burn_wielder: Burns the hand that holds it (%s)
tooltip.feedback.attuned.ignite_attacker: Sets whoever strikes the wearer alight (%s)
message.feedback.mixer.refused: The drum takes any material, up to a full load.
message.feedback.mixer.frozen: A molten metal in the drum has set solid: heat the drum before drawing.
message.feedback.mixer.draw_blocked: Nothing to draw, or the last draw is still waiting at the output.
feedback.jei.info.mixer: A drum on a vertical shaft. Right click with an item to pour one in; items from a hopper or the input slots go in one at a time while there is room. A fluid with a material (molten metals among them) is a part of the mixture too, from a pipe. Turning mixes them: draw too early and only the mixed share is kept; keep turning past the blend and the drum grinds it, heats it, and a powder load goes up. Draw with the button in the screen; the mixture table decides what the batch becomes, and a batch no row names comes out as a Mixture item.
feedback.jei.info.smithing_table: Where metal parts are shaped: pick a part, put stock in its cells, and spend a point of a Hand Hammer from its slot. Stock must be at its working temperature.
feedback.jei.info.anvil: The Smithing Table's upgrade: it shapes metal the same way and also forges, playing a rhythm pattern for the forged variant of a part. Set a Hearth against it on a lit fire to keep the stock hot while you play. A bloom set in the center is shingled here: strike it hot to squeeze the slag out, turn it to herd the rest. Repair, rename and combine are not done here.
feedback.jei.info.woodworking_table: Where wood, bone, leather, fiber and paper parts are shaped. Pick a part, put stock in its cells, and spend a point of an axe from its slot.
feedback.jei.info.stonecutter: Where stone, ceramic, glass and crystal parts are shaped. Pick a part, put stock in its cells, and spend a point of a Sawblade from its slot. A cut made with a Data Stick in the off hand is recorded for a Power Cutter.
feedback.jei.info.prep_table: Where dishes are made. Pick a dish, put food in its cells, and cut with a knife from its slot.
feedback.jei.info.blueprint_table: Draw a modular item here and print it on paper. The blueprint predicts the figures the parts would give if they came out exactly to drawing; what an item really has is read off the item with an instrument. A second slot beside the paper holds a blueprint to copy: press Copy with blank paper in the paper slot and the original stays.
feedback.jei.info.enchanting_table: Open it with a part to enchant. The part is held while the screen is open and handed back when it closes.
feedback.jei.info.reloading_press: Use it to open it. Seat a bullet and a charge in a case to make a cartridge. The bullet's shape is the bullet you seat. A nugget makes buckshot; birdshot, large shot and flechettes are their own items. A nugget in the core slot sits inside a bullet's jacket. A brewed potion in the payload slot is sealed in a glass vial in the bullet and let go where the round lands. A seed, a strand of string or a lump of slime also go in the payload slot.
feedback.jei.info.firebox: A brick hole with a fire in it. Right-click with fuel to load it, and with an empty hand to take back fuel that has yet to catch. Set a Crucible or Boiler on top and it climbs toward the flame's temperature. Only real fuels burn here, by what they are made of.
feedback.jei.info.stockpot: A pot, made from five plates of one metal in a U; the metal sets how fast it follows its fire. It cooks a batch over a lit Firebox. Pour in up to two water buckets, add up to six foods raw or cooked, shake in salt, and ladle out bowls with a bowl in hand. Stir and skim with a spoon, and read it with an empty hand; sneak with an empty hand to tip it out, which burns if the pot is hot.
feedback.jei.info.drying_rack: A rack that dries food slowly. Right-click with a food to hang it, up to four, and right-click empty-handed to take the last one back. Dried food feeds less but keeps much longer; drying runs faster in warm air, and rain stops it, so put a roof over it.
feedback.jei.info.hearth: A brick pan that keeps an Anvil hot. Set it on a Firebox or any fire with an Anvil against one of its sides, and light the fire. The pan warms to about nine tenths of the fire's heat, so hot-working stock in the Anvil stays workable while you forge.
feedback.jei.info.ice_box: A chest that keeps food cold for as long as it has ice. Put ice in with the food; it melts away in about ten minutes. A Refrigeration Unit set against the box and wired up holds it near freezing with no ice used.
feedback.jei.info.controller: A mechanical logic box that reads sensors, compares numbers and switches things on or off. Write a program onto a Punch Card at the Programmer, then right-click the Controller with the card to load it. It is the step up from a Timer or Bimetallic Strip.
feedback.jei.info.programmer: Where Controller programs are written onto Punch Cards. Different programmers write onto different things and make changes at different ease, but every one says the same things. Write the program, then load the printed card into a Controller.
feedback.jei.info.thermometer: Turns glowing orange into a number. Carry it and the temperature of items and blocks shows in tooltips and Jade, in steps of 25 Tu. A Pyrometer reads a vessel from further away.
feedback.jei.info.pyrometer: A Thermometer with a lens in it. Right-click a vessel up to 24 blocks away to read its temperature in steps of 10 Tu, whether the furnace is sealed or open.
feedback.jei.info.pressure_gauge: Turns the boiler is groaning into a number. Right-click a boiler, vessel, pipe or tank to read its pressure in steps of 0.5 Pu.
feedback.jei.info.geiger_counter: Listens for radiation. It clicks a few times a second with nothing near and faster the stronger the field. Carry it to see the rate in Ru from the last five seconds of clicks; it reads the field before your armor, so it shows why to shield.
feedback.jei.info.dosimeter: Reads the dose you carry, the running total that makes you ill in steps. The dose builds while you stand in radiation and drops once you leave it.
feedback.jei.info.temperature_sensor: A thermometer bolted onto a crucible or Improved Furnace. It reads the vessel's temperature all the time in steps of 10 Tu, and a Controller program can act on that reading.
feedback.jei.info.electroscope: Two thin copper foil leaves in a glass jar that spread apart when they touch something charged. It reads voltage in steps of 0.5 V, and it is a deliberately rough instrument and the cheapest electrical one.
feedback.jei.info.galvanometer: A needle that swings when current runs through it. Hold it near a block in a circuit to read how much current flows through it, in steps of 0.25 A.
feedback.jei.info.current_sensor: A small galvanometer bolted onto one face of a Copper Cable. It reads the current through that cable all the time, in steps of 0.5 A, so a Controller program can act on it.
feedback.jei.info.balance_scale: Tells exactly how heavy a tool, weapon or piece of armor is, in tenths of a Mu. The tooltip gives a rough word for weight, and the scale gives the number.
feedback.jei.info.survey_meter: Shows the ore and oil within 16 blocks, so you can dig where the ground holds them. It needs no power, and its counts are rounded to 8 and wobble a little.
feedback.jei.info.xp_meter: Reads experience as numbers: the level something stands at and the points it holds. Right-click a Crystal Holder, an XP wire, a Creative XP Source, the air, a player or a villager to read it.
feedback.jei.info.burner: A burner for liquid and gas fuel, fed by a pipe or bucket. It heats whatever sits on top, a Crucible, Boiler or Reactor, toward the flame's temperature. It holds 2000 mB and burns 10 mB a second whenever it has fuel; any fluid that burns will do. Built from a nozzle part: its bore sets the fuel burned, its shape the flame; an optional flame holder runs a little hotter.
feedback.jei.info.breaker: A switch for electricity. Closed, it is a piece of wire; open, the line is split in two. Right-click to open or close it, or let a Controller switch it with a Switch card. Above 4 A it trips itself open until someone closes it by hand. Built with cables in place of the copper wire, it takes their gauge and trips at that cable's rating.
feedback.jei.info.bellows: Blows air into whatever it touches, and air makes a fire burn hotter. Drive it with a Crank Linkage, set it in front of the linkage, and touch it to a Firebox, a furnace, a valve or a Pressure Vessel. It is the only way past a fuel's normal temperature.
feedback.jei.info.bimetallic_strip: Two metals bonded together that bend when hot. Clip it to a Crucible and anything it touches switches on while the crucible is below its trip temperature and off above it. Set it against the thing to switch, such as a Clutch or Valve.
feedback.jei.info.compressor: Squeezes gas into a pipe or Gas Tank past the point where it flows by itself, raising a line's pressure. Place it against the block it draws from, with its shaft across the flow. It moves gas only, at 0.4 mB a tick for every RPM, and heats what it moves. Built from a rotor part (Chemical Treatise II): diameter and staging set flow, load and heat; an optional intercooler cools the gas.
feedback.jei.info.damper: A vent flap built against a Crucible, the opposite of the Powered Bellows. Open, it lets heat out at twice what a bare crucible loses, and up to four count. Right-click to open or close it, or let a Timer, Bimetallic Strip or Controller do it.
feedback.jei.info.electromagnet: The first machine that runs on electricity. While powered it pulls nearby dropped iron, steel, cast iron, hardened steel and netherite items toward itself, in any form. Eight Copper Wire wrapped around a Wrought Iron Ingot make one. Built from a core part: turns set pull and current, shape trades pull against reach; an optional yoke adds pull.
feedback.jei.info.lamp: Vanilla's redstone lamp is a block lit by a redstone signal. This one is an electroluminescent glowstone panel: a 0.5 A load on a 6 V power line that glows in four steps (off, dim, bright, full) by how well it is fed, and keeps its step steady near a boundary. Too little voltage only dims it. Mild overvoltage wears it dimmer for good; twice its rated volts burns the panel out at once. Built from a filament part: thickness sets the draw and the life; an optional ballast rides overvoltage.
feedback.jei.info.gas_tank: A big pressure vessel for gas, a shell built like the Pressure Vessel's but many times the size. Its metal, wall and shape set how much it holds and the pressure it risks letting go at. Plain flow fills it to four fifths of its danger line and a Gas Compressor fills it higher. Right-click with an empty hand to read its contents and pressure. Optional addons: hoop bands and a relief valve, as on the Pressure Vessel.
feedback.jei.info.gas_turbine: A rotation source that burns fuel gas continuously. At full spool it turns 240 RPM and supplies up to 300 Su on its shaft. It needs blades before it runs, takes fuel from any fluid tank or pipe touching it, and a hotter fuel gives more power for less.
feedback.jei.info.heat_exchanger: A wall that carries heat from the hotter thing on one side to the cooler thing on the other, faster the bigger the difference, until they level. Built at a Smithing Table from a blueprint drawn at the Blueprint Table (Chemical Treatise II): the tube metal's conductivity and the area you give it set how fast. Finned tubes present more area. It needs no power, switch or setting: place it with a thermal block on each end of its axis. An optional fin stack of a second metal adds to the heat that crosses.
feedback.jei.info.hand_crank: The simplest source of rotation. Hold right-click to keep it turning, and it coasts down when you let go. It delivers 12 Su at 32 RPM, enough for the lightest work; the workshop machines need more than a crank can give. Built from a crank arm: a longer arm is more Su and slower; an optional flywheel steadies it.
feedback.jei.info.leyden_jar: A glass jar lined with foil that stores a charge, built at a Stonecutter from a blueprint drawn at the Blueprint Table. More plate area holds more charge; thinner glass holds more again but leaks it away much faster. The glass must insulate. Optional addons: foil whose metal sets how hard it discharges, and a glass sleeve that slows the leak.
feedback.jei.info.overspeed_trip: A clutch with spinning weights inside that throws itself open if its shaft turns faster than its fitted spring allows (light 48, medium 120, heavy 300 RPM; sneak and right-click swaps the spring). Everything downstream coasts down on its own momentum, and it stays open until someone resets it. Place it inline on a shaft like any clutch.
feedback.jei.info.pressure_vessel: A sealed tank that a Powered Bellows pumps air into, built at a Smithing Table from a blueprint drawn at the Blueprint Table. The shape, the wall and the metal set how much pressure it holds and how much room is inside: a thicker wall holds more and leaves less, a sphere carries more than a cylinder, a flat box least. Up to its danger line it holds indefinitely; over that it may explode, and well over it certainly does. Read the gauge by using it. Optional addons: hoop bands raise the danger line; a relief valve vents air near it so a pump cannot burst the tank.
feedback.jei.info.pump: Moves fluid from its back to its front while its shaft turns: water, steam, molten metal or any other fluid. It moves 0.5 mB a tick for every RPM. Place it against the block it draws from, with its shaft across the flow. Built from an impeller part: its diameter and shape set flow, load and lift; an optional volute adds flow.
feedback.jei.info.steam_turbine: Turns hot steam into rotation at factory scale: about 16 kW (64 Su at 240 RPM) from 100 mB of steam a tick, which takes several boilers. Feed it steam from a Pipe or a touching Boiler; hotter steam gives more output, and its exhaust is steam a Condenser can recover. A shaft connects at either end of its axle.
feedback.jei.info.steam_engine: Turns steam into rotation. Place it touching a Boiler and it draws steam by itself, running at 16 RPM with 64 Su while it has steam. Its small store carries it over a stutter, and a shaft connects at either end of its axle.
feedback.jei.info.timer: A wind-up timer that switches the switchable blocks touching it on when started, and off when it runs out. Sneak-right-click to choose a 2, 5, 10 or 20 second wind, right-click to wind and start it, and right-click again to stop it early.
feedback.jei.info.water_wheel: Free, continuous rotation from flowing water. Built at a Woodworking Table from a blueprint drawn at the Blueprint Table : a bigger wheel catches more water and turns slower for the same flow, more buckets take more of it, and a heavier rim has more momentum. It turns a few RPM for each side with moving water against it. Place it along the axis of its axle with flowing water on its sides. An optional rim ring of dense metal adds momentum.
feedback.jei.info.galvanic_cell: A zinc-copper battery giving a steady 1.1 V at 1 A that lasts indefinitely. Place it touching Copper Cable or a machine and it supplies power straight away, with no fuel, GUI or switch. One cell runs one Electromagnet at about three-quarters strength. Built from an anode part: its size and shape set the current and the life; an optional copper cathode adds current.
feedback.jei.info.sculk_relay: Made from a Relay Organ. Every relay within 24 blocks of another joins its run, with no wire between them and no line of sight needed, in the same dimension.
feedback.jei.info.data_sensor: Listens like a sculk sensor, within 8 blocks, and holds the last frequency it heard for two seconds. Link it to a Controller with a Data Connector and read it with a sensor card, for the frequency and for each channel's match.
feedback.jei.info.reboiler: The base of a Fractionating Column. Steam pumped into it lifts coke off the trays while it is under 420 Tu, and the heavy bottoms stay in it while only the light cuts leave.
feedback.jei.info.flare: A steel stack that burns off gas nobody wants. It is the safe vent for a line that makes more gas than you can use, since a burned gas stays out of the air.
feedback.jei.info.modular_blueprint: A design on paper, printed at the Blueprint Table. Some types, the crossbow among them, take one at a bench's blueprint slot to be made.
feedback.jei.info.magazine: Put a magazine in the crafting grid with loose cartridges of one bore to fill it, as many as it has room for. Swap it into a gun by reloading.
feedback.jade.radioactive: Gives off %s Ru at point blank
feedback.jade.shielded: Lead-lined: what it holds does not radiate
feedback.survey.none: Nothing within reach reads above the noise.
modular.feedback.desc.part.box_feed: A well under a bolt or lever action that takes a box magazine. Without it the action loads one round by hand.
message.feedback.transmission.no_design: A transmission with no design has nothing to shift.
feedback.gloss.cut: reads up to %1$s Qu, in steps of %2$s Qu
tooltip.feedback.role.substrate: The base a trace board is built on.
tooltip.feedback.role.solder: Pastes a trace board; heat the joint to set it.
tooltip.feedback.role.rectifier: A switching part: mount it on a trace board, or seat it in a cat's whisker detector.
tooltip.feedback.role.board: Mount a part, paste it with solder, then heat the joint: it becomes a circuit.
tooltip.feedback.role.circuit: Fit it on a cat's whisker detector's contact for a quieter, further-hearing report.
advancement.feedback.electronics.root.de: A circuit is a board with a switching part on it. First a base: grind a brick flat on a grinding wheel to get a substrate.
advancement.feedback.electronics.substra: Lay traces: a substrate and redstone dust in a crafting grid. Then put a coherer (no ore needed) on the board in the grid, and paste it with a tin ingot.
advancement.feedback.electronics.board.d: Heat a soldering iron at a fire. Hold the pasted board in the other hand, right-click, and drag the tip along the pads at a steady pace.
advancement.feedback.electronics.circuit: Fit it on a cat's whisker detector's contact and read it with a component tester.
feedback.circuit.lifted: Traces lifted: the circuit is dead
feedback.better_combat_notice: Feedback is borrowing Better Combat's animations. If something looks wrong, report it to Feedback, never to Better Combat's author.
skill.feedback.move.wall_run.desc: Cast: with a wall beside you, run along it for most of a second, the wall taking your weight; look steers, crouch drops you. Reads whether a wall is at your side and your sprint. Costs 20 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.vault.desc: Cast: spring off the shoulders of the nearest thing in front and land behind it; it is staggered by your mass pushed off it. Costs 25 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.slide.desc: Cast: from a sprint, skid low along the ground; every body in the way is tripped once, staggered by your mass (armor counts). Costs 15 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.smoke_step.desc: Cast: roll out of a cloud left where you stood; for three seconds anything inside it loses you as a target, unless it is already at your elbow. Costs 25 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.thick_smoke.desc: Rider: Smoke step's cloud is half again as wide and lasts five seconds.
skill.feedback.move.vanish.desc: Cast: invisible for about five seconds, less the more armor you wear (mass clanks); landing a blow gives you away. Reads worn armor mass. Costs 20 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.long_shadow.desc: Rider: Vanish lasts three seconds longer.
skill.feedback.move.pocket_sand.desc: Cast: throw a fistful of the ground at the eyes of a cone: loose sand blinds six seconds, dirt three, bare stone gives you nothing to throw. Targets lose you and flinch. Reads the block underfoot. Costs 15 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.grit.desc: Rider: Pocket sand blinds two seconds longer, and crushed stone underfoot will do.
skill.feedback.move.challenge.desc: Cast: ring your weapon on your guard; every hostile within ten blocks turns on you. The weapon pays a point of wear for the noise. Costs 15 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.advance.desc: Cast: for three seconds walk forward behind a held guard; everything in front is shoved back by the ratio of your mass to its, and the lighter ones are staggered. Needs a shield-type item. Costs 25 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.punish.desc: Cast: a heavy blow, over twice the weapon's damage, on the nearest thing in reach that is already staggered; nothing standing steady will take it. Rearms on a stagger. Costs 25 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.rebuke.desc: Always on: every melee blow you take is struck back at the attacker for six tenths of what it dealt. You still take all of it.
skill.feedback.move.rising_tempo.desc: Always on: with bare hands or a quick weapon (the tempo of a dagger or faster), each blow you land within a second and a half of the last is fifteen percent harder than the one before, to eight deep. A pause breaks the chain.
skill.feedback.move.frenzy.desc: Cast: with bare hands or a quick weapon, swing eighty percent faster for five seconds; afterwards three seconds of swinging a third slower, winded. Costs 30 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.haymaker.desc: Cast: wind up for half a second, then one punch for nine damage, plus the fist damage of a worn plate, that shoves a body back by your mass over its. A miss leaves you staggered. Costs 30 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.stomp.desc: Cast: your whole weight on the nearest staggered thing in reach, as damage and a fresh stagger. Nothing standing steady will take it. Rearms on a stagger. Costs 20 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.crush.desc: Rider: Stomp hurts half again as much.
skill.feedback.move.axe_kick.desc: Cast: an overhead heel on the nearest thing in front; a raised guard is broken and its bearer staggered by your mass. Costs 25 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.rending_heel.desc: Rider: Axe kick also wears the target's armor, a heel's hardness against each piece's.
skill.feedback.move.bowling.desc: Throw upgrade: the thrown body flies as a ball for 25 ticks; everything it strikes is staggered by its mass (BodyMass, plus armor), and it takes the knocks too. Heavier bodies stagger harder. Price: the body is hurt by each strike.
skill.feedback.move.cleave.desc: Cast: raise a heavy weapon (damage 5 or more) and bring it down; the target takes the blow and a crack runs seven blocks on, staggering by the weapon's damage and fading with distance. Costs 30 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.dazzle.desc: Rider: Muzzle flash blinds for six seconds.
skill.feedback.move.concussive.desc: Rider: Muzzle flash staggers half again as hard.
skill.feedback.move.scorch.desc: Rider: Kindle and Searing strike leave their targets burning twice as long.
skill.feedback.move.called_shot.desc: Cast: the round is aimed not at where the thing under your crosshair is but at where its motion puts it by the time the round arrives. Needs line of sight, forty blocks at most. Costs a round, its heat and 25 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.point_blank.desc: Cast: fire into a body you hold or one already staggered within reach; the round's whole impulse is stagger and, past ten joules to the point, damage. Costs a round and 25 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.snap_volley.desc: Cast: up to three rounds, four ticks apart, each at the next nearest living thing in the forward cone. The gun's own cycle may refuse a follow-up; each round spends ammo and adds heat. Costs 30 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.human_shield.desc: Cast: the body you hold takes every blow aimed at you for as long as you hold it. If it dies, so does the cover. Needs a hold (Grab). Costs 20 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.disarm_shot.desc: Cast: a round aimed at the weapon hand of whoever you face within twenty blocks; if it leaves the muzzle, what they held falls at their feet and they flinch by the round's impulse. Costs a round and 25 stamina.
skill.feedback.move.field_dressing.desc: Held cast: stand still and hold the key to bind your wounds. Health comes back while you hold it, and stamina drains 25 a second, so a full bar buys about four hearts. Moving, taking damage, full health or an empty bar ends it: it is for between fights. Rearms on the clock.
skill.feedback.move.second_breath.desc: Cast: a deep breath that refills stamina to sixty and pauses its regen, as a rest does. Worn armor presses on the chest: heavy plate breathes to about forty. Costs no stamina; rearms when you land a blow.
skill.feedback.move.shake_off.desc: Cast: a hard full-body shake. If you are burning it beats the fire out; otherwise it clears the harmful effect with the most time left. One thing per cast. Rearms when you stagger something.
skill.feedback.move.wind_back.desc: A parry landed while your stamina is under 30 gives 15 back, without pausing regen. Price: you have to be low and still parry; rearms on the clock.
skill.feedback.move.grit_teeth.desc: Always on: every blow you take lands lighter by a share read off the armor you wear (15% bare, up to 55% in full plate), for 10 stamina a blow. With less than that in the bar the blow lands whole.
skill.feedback.move.break_free.desc: Shake off first throws off any rope someone else has on you (a grab, a hooked weapon) and staggers whoever held it, by their mass. Your own grapple is left alone.
skill.feedback.move.tend.desc: Held cast: stand still within two blocks of an ally who is hurt, and hold the key to bind their wounds. They mend as fast as Field dressing mends you, and stamina drains from you, 25 a second. Either of you moving, either taking damage, the ally at full health or an empty bar ends it. Rearms on the clock.
skill.feedback.move.hand_off.desc: Cast: pass stamina to an ally within three blocks. You spend 30; 60% of it reaches them, the rest is lost in the handing over. Rearms on the clock.
skill.feedback.move.cut_loose.desc: Cast: cut an ally within five blocks free of every rope someone else has on them (a grab, a hooked weapon) and break the grab on them, staggering the holder by their mass. Costs 20 stamina; rearms on the clock.
skill.feedback.move.callused_hands.desc: Bare hands take the scald band: anything under 300 Tu can be held or touched unhurt. Burning and searing still hurt; gloves and tongs still do better.
skill.feedback.move.sear_shut.desc: A Cauterize with a piece hot enough to sear also clears the harmful effect with the most time left. Price: the sear's own burn and fire.
skill.feedback.move.blood_up.desc: Three empty-hand hits, each within three seconds of the last, with no damage taken between, heal one heart. Taking a hit breaks the run. Rearms on the clock.
skill.feedback.move.breather.desc: A kill with a modular weapon in your main hand gives back stamina by the weapon's mass: 10 a Mu, between 10 and 40. A heavy weapon earns a deep breath.
skill.feedback.move.cauterize.desc: Cast: press a hot piece from either hand to the wound. A piece hot enough to burn heals three hearts, one hot enough to sear heals six, and you take that band's burn and catch fire. The piece comes away 200 Tu cooler. Needs something at least burning hot in hand.
screen.feedback.skills.equip.tip.key: Press to slot the picked technique.
gui.feedback.notes.title: Reading the specimen
gui.feedback.notes.hint: Click to open the calipers and move the mouse; click again when the jaws just touch the part. Tight crushes the reading, loose is a guess.
gui.feedback.upset.title: Rivet
gui.feedback.upset.hint: Hold the mouse to raise the hammer. Let go to strike. Aim for the green band: lighter leaves the head loose, harder flattens it and splits it. Hard metal wants a harder blow in a narrower band.
gui.feedback.torque.title: Torque
gui.feedback.torque.hint: Hold the mouse to wind the driver. Let go inside the green band. Past it the thread strips.
gui.feedback.fitting.title: Fitting
gui.feedback.fitting.hint: Watch the bench work the part, then repeat the strokes: click the tools or press 1 to 4. A wrong stroke ends the fitting where you got to; the grade only sets how well the assembly starts.
gui.feedback.engineering.note.no_tool: Needs a hammer in the tool row
gui.feedback.engineering.note.nothing: Nothing in the stock does anything
gui.feedback.engineering.note.no_blank: Needs a blank treatise or blank paper
gui.feedback.engineering.note.dish: A dish is taken apart at the Prep Table
gui.feedback.engineering.tip.tool: Hand tool: a hammer, saw, file or screwdriver. Wears with use.
gui.feedback.engineering.tip.fastener: Fixings: screws, machine bolts or rivets. Spent per assembly; better metal fits better.
gui.feedback.engineering.tip.blueprint: Blueprint: judges the fit and skips the hand work. Never required.
gui.feedback.engineering.tip.blank: A blank treatise or blank paper: the specimen's volume is written onto it.
gui.feedback.engineering.tip.binder: Treatise binder: its volumes count as known here.
feedback.jei.info.engineering_table: Where parts are put together. Four tabs. Crafting: lay the parts in the 3x3 grid (positions do not matter), hand tools in the tool row (a hammer, saw, file or screwdriver; each craft wears the ones it needs a point, and a broken tool stays in its slot and blocks the craft until it is reworked) and fasteners in the fastener row (screws, machine bolts or rivets; the metal sets their quality, and better than the work asks gives a better start, worse still builds). A treatise binder in the corner counts its volumes as held. Most assemblies then ask for a hand-work game, torque or fitting, that scores the start only and never gates; a blueprint in the blueprint slot skips it. Fit: bolt several attachments onto a finished item at once. Repair: repair, swap a part or take an item apart. Treatise: copy a specimen onto a blank treatise. The part-making benches (Smithing Table, Anvil, Woodworking Table, Stonecutter) only make parts; the putting together is done here.

modular.feedback.desc.part.driver_bit: A hardened tip for a screwdriver. It wears with every turn.

feedback.jei.info.file: A hand tool for the Engineering Table's tool row (ability: file). Each craft that calls for a file wears it a point; a broken one stays in its slot and blocks the craft until it is reworked.
feedback.jei.info.screwdriver: A hand tool for the Engineering Table's tool row (ability: driver). Each craft that calls for a driver wears it a point; a broken one stays in its slot and blocks the craft until it is reworked.
feedback.jei.info.fastener: A fastener for the Engineering Table's fastener row. Its quality is read from its material (1 to 5): above a recipe's floor the finished item starts better fitted, below it still builds but worse.
modular.feedback.desc.part.saw_blade: A toothed plate for a sawblade. Its edge wears with every cut.

modular.feedback.role.container.tip: What the dish sits on, and what tells the table which dish it is: a bowl, a plate, a skewer or a baked flatbread. Its size caps how much meal there is and how long it takes to eat. Shaped at the Prep Table.
modular.feedback.role.base.tip: The bulk of the dish: a starchy food, such as a potato or bread.
modular.feedback.role.main.tip: The dense part: a protein, such as meat or fish. Every dish needs one.
modular.feedback.role.side.tip: Fiber and bulk: a plant food, such as a vegetable or fruit.
modular.feedback.role.finish.tip: A small, strong addition: a seasoning, such as honey. It moves the buff more than the hunger.
perk.feedback.settling.gloss: Eases nausea and food-poisoning sickness; strong cases are beyond it.
perk.feedback.warming.gloss: Stops the cold of powder snow from building up for a while; gives nothing against fire.
perk.feedback.cooling.gloss: Puts out burning sooner for a while; standing in lava still kills.
perk.feedback.antitoxin.gloss: Lowers the toxin in the same meal by a fraction; a deadly food stays deadly.
perk.feedback.antibiotic.gloss: Lowers the live pathogen in the same meal; rotten food is past help.
perk.feedback.antivenin.gloss: Eases poison I; stronger poison and wither are beyond it.
perk.feedback.sobering.gloss: Eases darkness, blindness and slowness up to level I.
perk.feedback.night_sight.gloss: Brief night vision, and blindness cannot land while it lasts; leaves you briefly slowed.
perk.feedback.fortifying.gloss: Lengthens the other effects of the same meal, up to double.
perk.feedback.slow_release.gloss: Stretches the meal's effects but holds them back longer.
perk.feedback.quickening.gloss: The meal's effects arrive sooner and end sooner, and a crash may follow.
perk.feedback.bracing.gloss: A small absorbing shield for a while, about one hit worth.
perk.feedback.mending.gloss: Heals you faster for a while, but only while you are fed.
perk.feedback.steadying.gloss: Blows push you less for a while; explosions still do. Slows you while it lasts.
perk.feedback.lightfoot.gloss: Brief speed and quicker stamina refill, at the price of hunger.
perk.feedback.bitter_tonic.gloss: Eases weakness and mining fatigue up to level I, then leaves a short slowness.
perk.feedback.brine_tolerance.gloss: Salt in the same dish protects it from spoiling longer; toxin is not helped.
perk.feedback.sleep_ward.gloss: Sets back the time since you last rested, so phantoms hold off; leaves you drowsy.
perk.feedback.breathing.gloss: Your air lasts longer underwater for a while; it is the air bar only.
perk.feedback.digestive.gloss: Fat and fiber hold the meal's effects back less, so they come sooner.
perk.feedback.hearth.gloss: A warm meal with this keeps you regenerating for longer; cold meals get nothing.
perk.feedback.keen_edge.gloss: Your blows land harder for a short while, but you are hurt more too.

feedback.jei.info.impact_pendulum: Right-click it with a tool or armour piece you made and the pendulum swings into the edge and reports its toughness, to the nearest 5. A twin-headed tool reports both heads. It leaves the piece unmarked.
feedback.jei.info.strike_post: Swing at it with a tool you made and it reports what the blow carries in joules and the damage it deals, to the nearest half. It leaves the tool unmarked.
feedback.jei.info.sheathed_billet: Calcined redstone-chromium powder packed in a silver sheath. Draw it down in three stages (roll to a rod, draw to a wire, draw to a fine wire), annealing after every stage: a cold stage strains the metal, one with no anneal behind it will not move. Each anneal taken at the limit adds a cycle of texture; one taken early adds nothing. Then a reaction anneal at about 880 Tu in oxygen at 3.8 to 4.6 Pu makes superconducting wire: three cycles for the best, two or one for a weaker, none for nothing.
feedback.grapple.tension.exact: Line load %1$s%% of its rating, strain %2$s%%
feedback.jei.info.sheave: A pulley wheel you set in the air. A grapple line that runs through it turns on it and goes on from there, and it does not saw the line the way a block's edge does. Hang a line from a ceiling beam or a post and swing round it.
feedback.jei.info.respirator: A leather mask with a charcoal filter, worn on the head. It cuts the dose from fumes and toxic clouds to a fifth. It filters, it does not supply air, and it never wears out.
feedback.jei.info.shock_capsule: A steel capsule packed with graphite, set off by a blast. A blast of the right size (a creeper, TNT, a respawn anchor) squeezes the carbon into 4 Diamond Grit. Too weak a blast leaves it whole. Too strong a one (a charged creeper, an end crystal) vaporises the carbon and it comes back as graphite.
feedback.jei.info.diamond_seed: A chip of diamond for a crystal to grow on. Cut two from a Diamond, or press eight Diamond Grit into one. In a hot Reactor it grows into a Diamond two ways: with graphite on an iron, nickel or cobalt bed, held just under the vessel's burst pressure with argon; or with a thin methane and hydrogen mix at about 880 Tu, which grows two. Too hot and either turns to graphite.
message.feedback.fuel_channel.rod: Rod burnt %1$s%%, condition %2$s%%. Sneak with an empty hand to take it out.
message.feedback.fuel_channel.empty: Empty channel. Put a fuel rod in.
message.feedback.control_assembly: Rods at %1$s of %2$s, set to %3$s. Click to step the target; absorber in hand loads it.
feedback.jade.fission.assembly: Rods at %1$s, set to %2$s, absorber strength %3$s%%
feedback.jei.info.reactor_core: The heart of a fission reactor. It sits at the top center of a shell seven blocks wide and seven tall: the six faces of the shell are walls of any dense material (lead, steel), the edges can stay open, and the five by five by five space under the core is the lattice. Put Fuel Channels, Control Rod Assemblies and Graphite Moderators in the lattice. The core makes heat only: put a Heat Exchanger beside it in the lid, with a Boiler on its far side, and the steam goes to a turbine. It cannot be switched off at once: decay heat keeps coming after the rods go in.
feedback.jei.info.fuel_channel: A lattice cell that holds one Fuel Rod. A rod beside a moderator or another rod runs hotter, a rod beside a control assembly cooler. Sneak with an empty hand to take the rod out.
feedback.jei.info.control_assembly: A bundle of absorber (cobalt, tungsten or lead) that sits at one of five positions, out to in. Click it to step its target, or wire it to a Controller switch. The core drops every assembly all the way in on a SCRAM.
feedback.jei.info.scram_trip: A passive safety. Built into the shell, it drops every control rod by itself once the core passes its trip temperature, with no power and no signal.
feedback.jei.info.graphite_moderator: Slows neutrons so the fuel beside it runs hotter. Read from graphite's own moderation figure, not its name.
feedback.jei.info.fuel_rod: Natural uranium clad in stainless steel. It burns for about two hours at full power, then becomes a Spent Rod.
feedback.jei.info.thorium_fuel_rod: Thorium and a little uranium. The thorium slowly breeds fissile material while it runs, so the rod lasts longer than a plain uranium rod.
feedback.jei.info.spent_fuel_rod: A burnt-out rod. Very radioactive: store it in a lead-lined chest.
feedback.jei.info.core_slag: What a breached core leaves behind. It stays radioactive for a long time and drops nothing.
message.feedback.magma_head.cold: Too cold to flow: fire %1$s Tu, bit %2$s%%.
message.feedback.magma_head.idle: Hot enough (fire %1$s Tu), but the shaft is still. Bit %2$s%%.
message.feedback.magma_head.flowing: Magma melt flowing, fire %1$s Tu, bit %2$s%%.
message.feedback.magma_head.blocked: Fire %1$s Tu, but nothing takes the melt. Bit %2$s%%.
feedback.jei.info.arc_hearth: A deep lined hearth: six charge slots and a 36-ingot tank, a crucible four times over. It has no fire of its own. Set an Arc Head on top of it and run an EHV line to the head; the plasma reaches about 3,500 Tu, enough to melt tungsten. Left running it boils volatile metals out of the bath, burns carbon out of steel, wears the electrodes and flashes. It also takes nitrogen or argon through its fluid face and holds it under the arc head: a sintering batch (the Heavy Core) spends that gas, and without it the batch is ruined.
feedback.jei.info.induction_coil: A coil around a crucible: a changing field heats the metal inside directly, with no flame and no smoke, up to about 1,800 Tu. It faces the way it was placed and needs a crucible holding metal (an ingot, scrap or a molten bath) in front of it; an empty crucible gets nothing. It draws 8 A at MV (6 V) while there is metal to heat and follows its power with some inertia.
feedback.jei.info.induction_stove: A hob for cookware: it heats a pan or pot set on top when the cookware is made of a magnetic material (iron and steel yes, copper and aluminum no), up to about 600 Tu, with no fire and no smoke. It draws 4 A at MV (6 V) only while magnetic cookware sits on it.
feedback.jei.info.preheat_coil: Right click with a piece to lay it in the coil, empty-handed to take it back. An empty hand on the empty coil, or sneaking, steps its target temperature (off, or 600 to 1,800 Tu). While powered at MV (8 A at 6 V) it brings a metal piece quickly to that target; it knows nothing of the piece's forging window, so matching the two is up to you. It holds the piece there while powered, and unpowered the piece cools in the coil as it would anywhere. Only metals heat.
feedback.jei.info.heavy_core: Dense as osmium, about three times iron, and hard to melt: it is pressed from osmium powder and sintered, never cast. It is the very block found in trial chambers, which the builders made the same way. Three green compacts sinter in the Arc Hearth at 1,800 to 2,150 Tu with nitrogen or argon held in its tank. In air the powder oxidizes to osmium tetroxide: the batch is lost and a cloud of toxic fume stays, which blinds, then burns the lungs of anyone who stays in it. Too hot and the grains coarsen, a weak porous sinter. A mace or maul head reads its density.
feedback.jei.info.arc_head: Three electrodes lowered into whatever it is set against: a crucible or an Arc Hearth. Right click with an electrode to fit one, empty-handed to take one back. It draws 42 A at EHV (384 V) with all three fitted and burns as hot as the supply and the weakest electrode allow. The head faces the block it was placed against.
feedback.jei.info.arc_electrode: A rod of a material that can carry the arc: graphite sublimes near 3,600 Tu, a conducting metal boils. The hotter and longer the bath, the faster it wears. A worn electrode snaps and drops into the bath.
tooltip.feedback.data_stick.assembly: Records an assembly of %1$s from %2$s kinds of stock.
tooltip.feedback.data_stick.blank: Blank. Hold it in your off hand while you make a cut at a Stonecutter to record that cut.
tooltip.feedback.data_stick.cut: Records a cut to %1$s from %2$s stock in the %3$s form.
tooltip.feedback.cutter_head: Takes stock up to hardness %1$s, condition %2$s%%
feedback.jei.info.auto_engineer: Plays back one hand assembly a recipe data stick recorded at the Engineering Table (hold a blank stick in your off hand while you take the crafted output there), on about 1 kW at EHV (384 V). Right click with a data stick to seat it, a hand tool (hammer, saw blade, file, screwdriver) for a tool slot, fasteners for its stock, anything else to fill the parts bay; empty-handed takes the output, then the stick; sneaking takes back tools, fasteners and parts. Hoppers fill the bay and the fastener stock and empty the output. Parts that match the stick are assembled at the floor quality, never better, and each assembly wears a point of the tools it needs and spends the fasteners; it waits when a tool is missing or broken. Parts the stick does not cover become something they could legally form (the same every time in a world), or scrap nuggets of their material with mass lost. Stock too hard, a full output, scrapping and an over-rated supply wear the machine; a correct assembly never does.
feedback.jei.info.power_cutter: Cuts what is fed to it, about twice a second, on about 1 kW at EHV (384 V). Right click with a cutter head or a recipe data stick to seat it, empty-handed to take the stick back, sneaking to take the head. Hoppers and pipes feed it and empty it. It does nothing without a head or without something to cut. Stock the stick recorded is cut the way it says; anything else gets a cut the machine could make, the same every time in a world, and what it cannot cut at all is lost. Stock harder than the head, a full output and an over-rated supply wear the head; correct cutting never does.
feedback.jei.info.saw_head: The cutting element of a Power Cutter for cold stock: stone, wood, ceramic, glass, crystal and bone. What it is made of sets the hardness it can take. A worn head cuts slower and never stops.
feedback.jei.info.plasma_head: The cutting element of a Power Cutter for conducting metal plate only: a plasma arc needs something to conduct. What it is made of sets the hardness it can take. A worn head cuts slower and never stops.
feedback.jei.info.data_stick: Blank until it records. Hold it in your off hand while you make a cut at a Stonecutter, or an assembly at the Engineering Table, and it keeps that work and the kind of stock it was made on. Seat it in a Power Cutter or an Auto Engineer to repeat it on stock of the same class. It holds one recording; making another overwrites it.

feedback.jade.icebox.hold.2: Held cold by the Refrigeration Unit
feedback.jei.info.refrigeration_unit: Against an Ice Box it holds the box cold. Against the inside of a walled room it holds the whole room cold: every Ice Box and loose item inside settles at the room's temperature. Walls leak by their material, openings (a gap, an open door, open sky) leak far more, and the unit draws more current the more the room leaks. Put a Condenser against the unit as a compressor stage and it can freeze: food held below freezing does not rot, and eats cold. Right-click with an empty hand to show where the room leaks.
feedback.jei.info.food_form: A whole block or rod of the foodstuff. It is edible (a mouthful for each raw item it holds), and it cooks, dries, chars and spoils in a furnace, a crucible or any pot the way the plain meat does.
feedback.jei.brewing_ingredient.note: Stirred at the Brewing Stand, it drags the marker along a curve in this direction. Cutting it at the Prep Table lengthens the curve; a hotter pot lengthens it too.
feedback.jei.brewing_ingredient.heading: Heads %s
feedback.jei.shape.line.tip: Straight to its end. The cheapest to stir for its reach.
feedback.jei.shape.arc.tip: Bows to one side on the way, then comes back to its heading.
feedback.jei.shape.wave.tip: Swings to both sides of its heading as it goes.
feedback.jei.shape.zigzag.tip: Cuts back and forth in sharp turns. Long to stir for its reach.
feedback.jei.shape.loop.tip: Doubles back on itself in a loop before running on to its end.
feedback.jei.shape.spiral.tip: Winds outward in turns and ends well off its heading. The longest to stir.
feedback.jei.shape.hook.tip: Runs straight, then bends sharply to one side at the end.
feedback.jei.info.brewing_stand: Right-click to open the stand's screen. Put a water bucket in the water slot, ingredients in the six slots and set it over a fire. Stir by circling the mouse over the map to walk the flask along the path the ingredients drew; the Pour button ladles water over the brew and sends the flask a step back toward the center. The compass trim shows each class's direction, and hovering an ingredient draws a ghost of its line. Cook ends the brew where the flask is: inside a node's ring a potion, anywhere else a dud draught.
feedback.jei.info.vacuum_dryer: Use a potion bottle on it to load it. It sits over a fire with a vacuum pump on a shaft: the faster the shaft turns, the deeper the vacuum. The potion dries once the chamber is warm enough and deep enough for a while, and stalls when either lapses. Too hot scorches away strength, far too hot cracks the bottle. An empty hand takes the salts out. Use salts on a water source to turn them back into a bottle, a little weaker.
feedback.jei.info.potion: Drink it for its effect, at the level and length it was brewed with; its potency fades with time, faster when warm. Sneak and use to throw it at a spot, where it splashes every creature nearby. Every potion can be drunk: fire sets the drinker alight and explosion bursts into heat on them.
feedback.jei.info.potion_use: Sneak and use with the bottle in one hand and a finished tool in the other to imbue it; its next few hits carry a short rider of the potion. Sneak and use a dish or serving with the bottle in the other hand, or pour it into a stockpot, to lace the food: the eater gets the effect without being told. A taste far from the food's own gives it away, and a nibble reports what it leans on.
feedback.jei.info.potion_salts: A bottle dried at the Vacuum Dryer. The salts never fade and keep the effect, level and strength they had when dried. Use them on a water source to reconstitute a bottle at a reduced strength.
feedback.jei.info.potion_salts_use: Salts cannot be imbued or poured into food; reconstitute them first.
feedback.jei.info.jar: Put one jar and one food, or one ladled serving, in the crafting grid in any arrangement to fill it. Then seal it in a Pressure Vessel over a hot fire.
feedback.jei.info.jarred_food: Made by filling a jar in the crafting grid. Heat above plain boiling, which only pressure reaches, seals it and kills what is live in it. Kept hot after sealing it goes mushy. Eating it returns the jar.
feedback.jei.info.salt: Left behind when a Stockpot of sea water boils dry beside the ocean or a beach, or dug from salt deposits crusted on the sand of ocean floors. Put one salt and one food in the crafting grid to salt the food: it keeps longer, is drier, and shrugs off more of what is live or toxic in it.
feedback.jei.info.dough: Three wheat and a water bucket. Knead it on the Prep Table, then bake it. Add an egg for pastry dough, or lay it out on the Prep Table for flatbread.
skill.feedback.figure.light_foot: Share %s of the movement-speed penalty your worn armor carries is handed back as speed
skill.feedback.figure.steady_walk: Spread that walking adds to a shot %s (fraction off)
skill.feedback.figure.footing: Crouched, a tether pulls you %s less (fraction off, more in heavy armor)
skill.feedback.figure.crank_beat: Each click on a loaded hand crank keeps it turning %s ticks longer
skill.feedback.figure.solder_braced: Soldering after lifting the iron crouched: the tip may stray %s pad pitches further before a joint bridges
skill.feedback.figure.solder_quiet: Soldering: the tip may stray %s pad pitches further before a joint bridges
skill.feedback.figure.step_hush: Your footsteps carry %s nearer to sculk sensors and wardens (fraction)
skill.feedback.figure.hand_hush: Breaking, placing, opening and pressing carry %s nearer to sculk sensors and wardens (fraction)
skill.feedback.figure.salvage_wear: Wear a part keeps when a tool is taken apart %s (fraction off)
skill.feedback.figure.charge_tamp: Power of a demolition charge you light %s (fraction)
skill.feedback.move.running_start.desc: A straight sprint builds speed, up to a quarter faster after three seconds. A hard turn or a stop lets it go.
skill.feedback.move.fleet.desc: Cast: a burst of speed for two and a half seconds, a trail of dust behind you. Sixty percent faster with no armor speed penalty; the more speed your worn armor costs, the less of the gain you keep, down to a fifth of it. Costs 20 stamina, and rearms when you land a blow.
skill.feedback.move.quick_draw.desc: Cast: the first gun in your hotbar comes up and fires on the same tick, and stays in your hand. If it cannot fire (empty, unchambered, still cycling, no gun in the hotbar) nothing is spent. The snap shot spreads wider the heavier the gun is against your own body mass, and a hot barrel adds its own bloom. Costs 20 stamina, and rearms when you land a blow.
skill.feedback.figure.fume_soften: Poison from a fume dose %s (fraction off)
feedback.fume_cloud.1: Your eyes sting and your head swims. Get out of the fumes.
feedback.fume_cloud.2: Your sight is going. Get out of the fumes.
feedback.fume_cloud.3: Your lungs burn. Get out of the fumes.
skill.feedback.figure.food_soften: Hazard effects of risky food %s (fraction off)
tooltip.feedback.potion_salts: Dissolve in a water source to restore a bottle, weaker than it was
feedback.jei.kind.metalloid.tip: An element between metal and salt. Cast like a metal, but brittle and a poor conductor.
message.feedback.creeper.sac_empty: Too little in the sac to cut a charge.
message.feedback.creeper.wont_eat: The creeper will not eat that.
tooltip.feedback.creeper.unstable: Goes off if shocked, burnt or sparked. Cut it with a hand knife.
tooltip.feedback.tasting.title: You taste %s:
feedback.jei.info.tasting_spoon: Hold a dish in one hand and use the spoon with the other to taste it: it names how hearty, rich, moist, done, salty, smoky, fresh, warm and what kind of food the dish is, the same things a villager judges. An instrument at the finest reading adds the figures. Each tasting wears the spoon.
modular.feedback.desc.part.spoon_bowl: The bowl of a spoon. A bigger bowl stirs a stockpot harder and skims more off the top.
feedback.jei.info.spoon: Aim at a stockpot and hold use to stir; tap use to skim the scum off the top. Stirring keeps the bottom from scorching and mixes the pot, but stirring with scum on top folds it in for good, so skim first. A bigger bowl does more per stroke. Every skim and a long stir wear the spoon, and stirring a pot hotter than the handle stands burns your hand.
modular.feedback.desc.part.spatula_blade: A broad flat blade for a spatula. Flips a piece in a skillet; held on the pan it lifts it off the fire.
feedback.jade.skillet.piece: Piece: %s Tu, cooked %s%%, moisture %s%%, char %s%% down, %s%% up
feedback.jade.stockpot.figures: Cooked %s%%, scum %s%%, mixed %s%%, water %s mB, solids %s mB
feedback.jei.info.skillet: A pan for cooking by hand, made from three plates of one metal over a stick; the metal sets how fast the pan follows the fire. Lay up to four pieces of food in it, one per quarter, and set it on a fire. Take a piece off with a bowl or plate to keep your hand safe. Grip it with tongs to lift it off the fire.
feedback.jei.info.spatula: Right-click a piece in a skillet to flip it. Only the face down chars, so turning evenly gives an even result. Each flip wears the spatula.
village.feedback.complaint.part: The %s is not what I asked for.
village.feedback.bar_tip: The cells show where in the usual range this lies.
village.feedback.hint.none: %s: no single material gets there; combine parts or reshape them.
village.feedback.hint.note: Each hint swaps one part of the plain design; the whole item is what is judged.
village.feedback.hint.dish: A tasting spoon reads a dish before you deliver it.
village.feedback.hint.fig.hunger: more food and a bigger container raise it.
village.feedback.hint.fig.fat: fatty foods (meat, nuts, butter) raise it; lean greens lower it.
village.feedback.hint.fig.fibre: whole, uncut plant food is chewier; cut it small and cook it to soften.
village.feedback.hint.fig.dish_moisture: wet foods and broths raise it; drying, baking and a sealed container change how it spreads.
village.feedback.hint.fig.dish_cook: cook the parts through before assembling; a pie bakes whole.
village.feedback.hint.fig.charred: less heat or less time keeps it down.
village.feedback.hint.fig.dish_salt: salted food and a salt part raise it.
village.feedback.hint.fig.dish_fresh: fresher parts, a quick delivery and a sealed container keep it up.
village.feedback.hint.fig.dish_warmth: deliver it hot from the fire; a warming container holds it.
village.feedback.hint.fig.share_seafood: more fish and seafood parts raise it.
village.feedback.hint.fig.share_plant: more vegetable, fruit and fungus parts raise it.
village.feedback.hint.fig.share_starch: more grain and dough parts raise it.
village.feedback.hint.fig.cuisine_italia: more parts that carry an Italian character.
village.feedback.hint.fig.cuisine_east_a: more parts that carry an East Asian character.
village.feedback.hint.fig.cuisine_mexica: more parts that carry a Mexican character.
village.feedback.hint.fig.cuisine_easter: more parts that carry an Eastern European character.
modular.feedback.fig.dish_cook.tip: How cooked through the dish is now.
modular.feedback.fig.dish_moisture.tip: The water in the dish now.
modular.feedback.fig.dish_smoke.tip: The smoke coat on the dish.
modular.feedback.fig.dish_fresh.tip: How fresh the dish is now; rot lowers it.
modular.feedback.fig.dish_warmth.tip: How warm the dish is now.
modular.feedback.fig.share_meat.tip: Share of the dish that is animal food.
modular.feedback.fig.share_seafood.tip: Share of the dish that is seafood.
modular.feedback.fig.share_plant.tip: Share of the dish that is vegetable, fruit or fungus.
modular.feedback.fig.share_starch.tip: Share of the dish that is grain or dough.
modular.feedback.fig.cuisine_italian.tip: Share of parts with an Italian character.
Share of parts with an East Asian character.
modular.feedback.fig.cuisine_mexican.tip: Share of parts with a Mexican character.
modular.feedback.fig.cuisine_eastern_eur: Share of parts with an Eastern European character.
modular.feedback.fig.charred.tip: How burnt the worst part is.
village.feedback.speech.wrong: That is not what I asked for.
feedback.jei.info.commissions: Villagers wanting a finished tool, weapon or armor piece of a type and quality post commissions each day. Put the piece in the delivery slot and press Deliver: the villager grades it on its true figures against what they asked, pays emeralds by class, and a slip tells you the one thing furthest off. Some wants are never said. Many deliveries of the same kind of piece in the same sort of material pay less for a few days.
gui.feedback.villager.sell_hint: Put what you want to sell in the slot.
village.feedback.speech.not_wanted: I am not buying that today.
village.feedback.speech.full: I have enough of those for today.
gui.feedback.mortar.hint: Grinding bowl: drop a plant in, then grab the pestle. Pound it to smash, rub it side to side to grind. Drag a plant out when it is as fine as you want.
feedback.jei.info.mortar: The heart of the Brewing Stand's grinding bowl, and an ingredient of the stand itself. At the stand, drop plants into the bowl and work them with the pestle: a plant ground finer gives the water more surface, so its compound comes out faster. Hard things need smashing; soft herbs grind easily.
gui.feedback.recipe.title: Recipe
gui.feedback.recipe.name_hint: Name it, or let it be named
gui.feedback.recipe.incomplete: A recipe needs a container and a main part.
message.feedback.arc_welder.no_power: No charged battery in your pack.
message.feedback.arc_welder.no_filler: No %s ingot in your pack for filler.
feedback.jei.info.arc_welder: Needs a charged battery and a filler ingot of the part's own material in your pack. Hold a worn tool, weapon, armor piece, gun or machine head in the other hand and hold right click to weld it; or right-click a worn machine with the welder. A weld restores the part to its best remaining condition, but each weld lowers that best by a step, down to a floor: a welded part is never as good as new. The electrode wears a little with every weld and keeps working.
modular.feedback.desc.part.backpack_shel: The body of a pack, worn on the back. Leather, cloth or sheet metal; its shape sets the slots: one cell a pouch, three a satchel, nine a pack. Add a strap to carry it.
modular.feedback.role.shell.tip: The bag body. Its shape fixes how many slots it holds; its material only decides how heavy it is.
modular.feedback.role.strap.tip: Carries the load. On a backpack its strength sets how much the wearer can carry before being slowed, and it is the part that wears and lets go. On a shield it carries the weight of the face, so the face holds a little more of a blow.
modular.feedback.fig.carry.tip: Mass of the pack and its contents the strap carries before the wearer is slowed and cannot sprint. Set by the strap's strength; falls as it wears.
modular.feedback.fig.slots.tip: Item slots of the bag, fixed by the shell's shape.
modular.feedback.role.hard_liner.tip: Two plates sewn inside the shell. The shell wears half as fast under an overload. Takes one mounting point.
