modular.feedback.role.fire_patch.tip: A plate over the shell's back. A burning wearer's cloth shell scorches without it, and wears; with it, not. Takes one mounting point.
modular.feedback.role.oiled_coat.tip: A hide soaked in oil and laid over the shell. A cloth shell without one soaks in water or rain and weighs half as much again. Takes one mounting point.
modular.feedback.role.warm_liner.tip: Three carpets quilted inside against the back: chill from powder snow leaves the wearer faster. Takes one mounting point.
modular.feedback.role.buckle.tip: A metal clasp on the chest strap. Its key drops the pack at once, contents and all. Takes one mounting point.
modular.feedback.role.lamp_bracket.tip: A rod hook above the pack: one slot that takes only a lantern. A lantern in it lights the way around the wearer. Takes one mounting point.
modular.feedback.desc.part.bedroll_sheet: The cloth or leather a bedroll is rolled in. Two cells. Add a fibrous fill and a leather shell.
modular.feedback.role.sheet.tip: What you lie on. Softer cloth or hide gives more comfort.
modular.feedback.role.fill.tip: Fibrous stuffing between the sheet and the shell. The softer it is, the better the sleep.
modular.feedback.role.pack_frame.tip: Four rods lashed to the shell. Rigid stock takes load off the strap and gives the pack more mounting points; it never wears.
modular.feedback.role.holster.tip: Two hides cut into a sleeve strapped outside: one tool or weapon, drawn without opening the pack. Takes one mounting point.
modular.feedback.role.bottle_loops.tip: A bundle of leather cut into loops: three small vessels (potions, flasks, fluid containers). Takes one mounting point.
modular.feedback.role.bandolier.tip: Two bundles of leather straps with loops: three slots for rounds and arrows. Takes one mounting point.
modular.feedback.role.hip_belt.tip: Three hides cut into bands that move the load to the hips; needs a frame to hang from. Its strength adds to the carry rating; it wears with the strap. Takes one mounting point.
modular.feedback.role.lashing.tip: Two sticks and a cord that tie a bedroll on top of the pack: one slot that takes only a bedroll. Takes one mounting point.
modular.feedback.role.panel.tip: Two carpets against the back. The softer the cloth the more it raises the carry rating. Takes one mounting point.
modular.feedback.role.pad.tip: Two boards that fold out into a bench: its key opens a 3x3 crafting grid while you stand on firm ground. Heavy, and takes two mounting points.
modular.feedback.fig.points.tip: Fittings take points from the shell (a pouch has the fewest, a pack the most); a frame gives more.
modular.feedback.fig.stores.tip: Typed slots the fittings add beside the fixed ones: holster, bottle loops, bedroll lashing, bandolier.
modular.feedback.fig.comfort.tip: How soft the fill and sheet are: the share of your health a night's sleep in it gives back.
message.feedback.pack_pad_ground: The pad needs firm ground under your feet.
message.feedback.bedroll.no_sleep: You can only bed down on firm ground at night or in a storm.
message.feedback.bedroll.not_safe: You cannot rest with monsters nearby.
feedback.jei.info.bedroll: Used on firm ground at night, or in a storm, with nothing hostile near, it skips to morning wherever you are and gives back health by its comfort (the softness of fill and sheet). It does not set your respawn point. Each night wears it. Carry it on a pack's bedroll lashing.
message.feedback.pack_strap_broke: The strap lets go and the pack falls away.
feedback.jei.info.backpack: Worn in the back slot; press the pack key to open it. The shell's shape fixes the slots (pouch 9, satchel 18, pack 27) and the strap's strength fixes how much the pack and its contents may weigh. Over that the wearer is slowed and cannot sprint, and the strap wears until it lets go and the pack falls off with everything in it. A pack cannot hold a pack. Rework the strap to mend it. Fittings are added at a Woodworking Table (a Smithing Table for plate fittings) by reworking a finished pack, and take mounting points from the shell (pouch 1, satchel 2, pack 4): a frame (four rods, gives 2 points, raises the rating), a hip belt (three hides, needs a frame, raises the rating), a padded panel (two carpets, softer is better), a side holster (two hides, one tool), bottle loops (a leather bundle, three vessels), a bandolier (two leather bundles, three slots for rounds and arrows), a bedroll lashing (two sticks, one bedroll; its key beds you down without taking the roll out), a crafting pad (two boards, two points, its own key opens a 3x3 grid on firm ground), a hard liner (two plates, the shell wears half as fast overloaded), a fire patch (a plate, keeps a burning wearer's cloth shell from scorching), an oiled coat (a hide, keeps a cloth shell from soaking), a warm liner (three carpets, thaws powder-snow chill), a quick-release buckle (a metal nugget; its key drops the pack at once) and a lamp bracket (a rod, one lantern slot that lights the wearer). Take a pack apart to remove a fitting.
message.feedback.tube.run: Tube run of %1$s blocks: %2$s of %3$s mB air, %4$s Pu
message.feedback.station: Address %1$s. Capsules %2$s, pods %3$s. Sort: %4$s. In bands: %5$s. Rejects: %6$s
feedback.jei.info.tube: A sealed pneumatic tube. A run of tubes shares one air ledger, and air pressure moves the capsules in it: a Compressor or the Creative Air Source pressurises the run, each hop spends a little air, and under a third of a Pu a capsule sits still until pressure returns. A heavy load slows a capsule, a bend slows it more, and a capsule too heavy for the bore stalls. Right-click to read the run's pressure. Over 5 Pu the run can burst.
feedback.jei.info.lined_tube: A tube with a smooth liner: less wall friction, so capsules move half as fast again at the same pressure.
feedback.jei.info.wide_tube: A wide-bore tube. Passes pods and far heavier capsules than the narrow tube. It joins narrow tubes freely, but a pod cannot enter a narrow one.
feedback.jei.info.evacuated_tube: A wide-bore tube sealed for vacuum. While its run is pumped down by a Vacuum Pump (under 0.05 Pu) capsules coast through at three times the plain speed with no air spent. Seals leak, so the pump must keep running; with the vacuum lost the tube behaves like a lined wide tube.
feedback.jei.info.tube_junction: Routes capsules by address, never by contents. Use a dye on a face to name the color that leaves that way (the same dye again clears it); sneak with an empty hand to clear all. A capsule with no matching color leaves by the first open face.
feedback.jei.info.programmed_junction: A junction that returns what it cannot place. Dye a face to name its color; click a face with an empty hand to make it the return line. A capsule with no matching color goes to the return line, and waits while that line is full rather than going astray.
feedback.jei.info.tube_station: The door of a tube run. Items fed in (by hopper or belt) are packed into a stocked capsule when the buffer is full or has stood idle, stamped with the station's address color, and sent into the tube it faces. Arriving capsules are emptied into an output buffer that pushes into neighboring inventories. Dye sets the address; sneak with an empty hand clears it. Use a capsule on the station to stock it. With the Sort Gauge it sorts at the door: each unit is read once and sent to one address if it is in the band, another if not. Sneak with a dye sets the in-band address.
feedback.jei.info.sorting_station: A tube station with up to three sort stages, each a separate reader (a magnet, an optical head or a weigher) that a unit must pass. Cargo it cannot place goes to the reject address (an off-hand dye sets it) instead of through. It runs at the pace of its slowest stage. The Sort Gauge adds and steps stages.
feedback.jei.info.sort_gauge: Use on a tube station to step the last sort stage through its bands and then its property; sneak to add a stage, or clear them when full.
feedback.jei.info.vacuum_pump: A shaft-driven pump that draws air out of the tube run it faces, with its shaft across the flow. An evacuated tube keeps its vacuum only while this keeps up with the seals' leak.
feedback.jei.info.linear_motor: A coil ring placed against a tube block. Fed with current it drives capsules that carry a magnetic plate through that block at twice the speed; plain capsules ignore it.
feedback.jei.info.carrier: A capsule that rides a tube. Holds four stacks and an address color; a heavy load slows it.
feedback.jei.info.magnetic_carrier: A capsule with a magnetic plate, the kind a linear-motor ring can drive.
feedback.jei.info.pod: A one-seat capsule for a wide-bore tube. Stock it in a tube station and right-click the station with an empty hand to board. Sneak to leave in an emergency: you step out at the tube. Pods are slower than capsules at the same pressure and slow down further in bends and vertical runs. Only players ride; a pod needs a wide-bore run all the way. If a chunk on the path is not loaded the pod waits for it.
feedback.jei.info.creative_air: Operator tab only. Compresses air at a set temperature, flow and pressure into any tube run, pipe run or gas tank beside it.
feedback.jei.info.ender_port: One end of a bonded pair: one pearl and two plates make two ports with the same bond. Items put in one cross to the other when the pair's per-minute mass allowance covers them and the tank holds enough liquid teleportant, which costs more for heavier items and longer distances. Both ends must be loaded; chunks are not loaded for it unless a Chunk Anchor is fitted. A shulker box next to the port seals it, and shulker boxes, fluid-holding items and pods never cross.
feedback.jei.info.ender_anchor: Use on an Ender Port to keep its chunk loaded so the pair works while nobody is near. Without it the pair pauses whenever an end is unloaded.
modular.feedback.desc.part.belt_band: The flexible strip a belt runs on. Its material sets how well cargo grips it and how hot the cargo may be; leather and rubber grip, a steel link band takes the heat. A textured face grips harder and a link band bends round hot cargo that would char a hide.
modular.feedback.role.band.tip: The strip cargo rides on. Its material sets the grip on a slope and the heat it takes.
modular.feedback.role.cleat.tip: Optional bars across the band. They roughen the face, so the belt holds cargo on a steeper slope.
feedback.jei.info.conveyor_belt: A belt cell built at a Woodworking Table (a Smithing Table for a steel link strip) from a band (leather, rubber or a steel link strip) with an optional cleat. Place cells end to end facing the same way, finish the run with a head roller, and turn the head's shaft: the run moves cargo at the shaft's speed. Sneak-click a cell with a belt in hand to make it climb or fall by one block; an empty hand sneak-clicks turns it. Cargo holds on a rise only while the belt's grip times the cargo's grip is enough, so a cleated or rubber band climbs where leather slips and a wet belt slips sooner. Hot cargo above the band's limit wears the band; a worn band slips but never fails. Dropped items that land on a belt ride it, and so do creatures. A coil block set on a belt heats what passes under it.
feedback.jei.info.belt_head: The driven roller at the exit end of a belt run; every other cell is an idler. Feed it a shaft from either side across the belt. The shaft's speed sets the belt's, and the load on the shaft is the roller's own plus the weight of the cargo on the run: an undersized shaft slows the whole belt.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_funnel_in: Fits into a belt cell and pulls items from the container on the side it was placed against, one unit at a time, as fast as the belt has room. It reads nothing about what it pulls.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_funnel_out: Fits into a belt cell and pushes passing cargo into the container on its side. At the end of a run a full container leaves the cargo queued on the belt.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_chute: Drops cargo off the belt, down the column below its side or into what is there: a container, a lower belt or the floor. Brittle cargo (low toughness for its hardness) breaks on a long drop.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_diverter: A plow that sweeps every unit that reaches it to its side. Empty-hand click engages or releases it; a controller can too.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_splitter: Sends passing cargo to alternate sides of the belt. If one side is full the other takes it.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_magnet: A permanent magnet over the belt. It sweeps magnetic cargo to its side and misses cargo above its Curie temperature or made of a non-magnetic metal; it will pull iron junk just as readily. Cargo it cannot place passes by.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_electromag: A switchable magnet drawing a little current. Stronger than a permanent one, it can be released by hand or by a controller. Cargo it cannot place goes to the opposite side.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_screen: A mesh the cargo passes over. Units lighter than the aperture fall through; click to choose fine, medium or coarse. Fines clog the mesh and blind it until it is wiped by hand.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_air_jet: A nozzle blowing light, dry cargo off the belt. It needs a gas pipe with pressure beside it and takes a little air with each puff; the pressure sets how dense a unit it can lift. Damp or sticky cargo stays put.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_optical: Reads the sheen of passing cargo and sweeps one band (dull, mid or bright) to its side. Click to choose the band. Glowing-hot cargo reads bright, and a dirty head reads everything duller until wiped. Cargo it cannot place goes to the opposite side. Draws a little current.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_weigher: Reads the weight of passing cargo: density bands and size bands. A stack blurs the reading because it weighs the pile. Click to choose the band. Cargo it cannot place goes to the opposite side. Draws a little current.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_counter: Counts what passes and reports the count and rate to a linked controller. It controls nothing and reads nothing about the cargo.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_cooler: A cold plate under which cargo cools toward a window, as a hot ingot must before it meets a leather band.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_gate: Holds cargo at its cell until released. Empty-hand click or a controller releases it.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_hood: A cover over a belt cell. Rain and fluid above no longer wet the band there, so a rise holds its grip; a unit carrying fluid still wets it.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_linear: A coil in place of a roller. While it has current it drives the whole run at a fixed speed, with or without a head roller or shaft. Draws a little current.
feedback.jei.info.belt_module_fan: Blows air over passing cargo and cools it. Draws a little current.
feedback.jei.ore_processing.separate: Separate: wash, magnet or optical sorter
feedback.jei.ore_processing.leach: Leach in the Reactor, then win the metal
tooltip.feedback.bloom.slag.0: Clean: hardly any slag left in it.
tooltip.feedback.bloom.slag.1: A little slag in the iron.
tooltip.feedback.bloom.slag.2: Plenty of slag in the iron.
feedback.jei.info.puddling_furnace: A reverberatory hearth with a rabble turned by a shaft into its back. Load cast iron and an oxidiser (hematite, magnetite, limonite or burnt iron scale), light it and keep it between 1250 and 1450 Tu while the shaft turns it at 20 to 60 RPM. Stalled or racing, the charge crusts and the hold falls back. Past 1500 the oxidiser eats the iron and leaves burnt iron. The ball it gives is a bloom with little slag in it: shingle it at an Anvil or under a Mechanical Hammer.
feedback.jei.info.iron_bloom: Spongy iron with slag trapped between its grains, made by heating iron ore with charcoal between 1000 and 1350 Tu (above that it carburises into cast iron) or by puddling cast iron. Put it hot in the center of an Anvil with a hammer and shingle it: strike to squeeze the slag out through the edges before the piece cools, and turn it to herd the rest. A Mechanical Hammer beating a bloom hot drives the slag out unattended.
feedback.jei.info.bloomery_slag: The slag a bloom gives up when it is worked. It still holds some iron: crush and melt it for pig iron.
screen.feedback.shingle.hint: Click to strike (right click for a heavy blow), R turns the piece, Space puts the hammer down. Squeeze the slag out to the edges while it is runny.
forge.feedback.shingle.done: The slag is out: wrought iron.
forge.feedback.shingle.left: Slag still in it. Reheat the bloom and work it again.
feedback.jei.info.redstone_emitter: Turns a data signal into redstone. A controller, timer or sensor program switches it like any actuator; engaged, it puts a full-strength redstone signal out of every face, so a vanilla piston, lamp or door can follow a Feedback sensor.
feedback.jei.info.analog_adapter: A fitting for a machine with a variable setting, such as a valve's opening or an engine's throttle. Right-click a face of the machine with it; redstone power arriving at that face then sets the setting from none to full in fifteen even steps: power 15 is full, power 0 is none. Take it off with a crowbar, and the machine returns to full. Any machine with a switch also starts and stops from redstone directly, with no adapter.
feedback.jei.info.ripeness_probe: Reads how grown the crop in front of it is, in quarters, from the crop's own age. A row of them sees a field. It reads any block that has an age, so a modded crop works too.
feedback.jei.info.photocell: Reads the light at the block in front of it, in fifths: the brighter of daylight and block light. It reads its own lamp as well, so a lamp it switches can switch it back.
feedback.jei.info.presence_plate: Reads whether a creature or a dropped item stands in the block in front of it: full when one does, nothing when not.
feedback.jei.info.fill_gauge: Reads how full the inventory or tank in front of it is, in eighths.
feedback.jei.info.note_block: Makes no sound on its own: fit a noisemaker (use it with one in hand; sneak with an empty hand takes it out). The noisemaker sets the instrument, the pitch is the note, 0 to 24: use with an empty hand to step it. A rising signal or a punch plays it.
feedback.jei.info.piston: Redstone only carries a signal, so a signal alone does not move a piston: each stroke out also uses 50 mB of gas from a gas tank, pressure vessel, compressor or pipe touching it on any face but the front. Without air it does not move.
feedback.jei.info.dropper: A spring pushes the item out, not the signal: a redstone signal only releases a cocked spring, and the spring stays spent afterwards. Cock it again by sneaking and using it with an empty hand, or by touching a turning shaft. A signal on a spent spring only clicks.
feedback.jei.info.dispenser: A dropper with a fitting that uses the item: arrows are fired, buckets emptied, fire charges lit, as in vanilla. Like the dropper, a signal only releases a cocked spring. Cock it by hand (sneak and use with an empty hand) or with a turning shaft.
feedback.jei.info.hopper: Carries one item at a time from the container above (or an item lying on it) into the block it faces, and holds nothing itself: if the block it faces cannot take the item, nothing moves. A chain of hoppers is a conveyor, not a store or a sorter. A redstone signal switches it off.
feedback.jei.info.observer: Reads high for half a second after the block in front of it changes state, such as a crop growing a stage or a door opening. It reports the change a tick late.
feedback.jei.info.pivot_mast: A vertical shaft whose arm sweeps a circle. Seat an arm (its length is the field's radius), a tip, and for the cutting, breaking and striking tips a machine head from a Smithing Table; put seed or feed in by hand or hopper and take what the collecting tip gathers from the other slots. The tip works every cell the arm crosses, along its whole length, and knows nothing about the job: a cutting tip cuts green crop as readily as ripe, so switch the drive with a ripeness probe. A long arm with a heavy head asks for more Su than a weak drive gives. Sneak with an empty hand to take parts back; an empty hand reads the arm and the head's condition.
feedback.jei.info.pivot_arm: An arm for the pivot mast. Its length in blocks (short 3, medium 5, long 8) is the radius of the field it sweeps, and the drive load grows with it.
feedback.jei.info.pivot_tip_cut: Cuts plants, leaves, cane, kelp and the wool of sheep along the pivot arm. Needs a machine head seated in the mast; one too soft for the target cuts nothing.
feedback.jei.info.pivot_tip_break: Breaks blocks along the pivot arm that the seated head can overcome. A block too hard for the head does not break, and the head wears by the difference. Machines and chests are left standing.
feedback.jei.info.pivot_tip_plant: Places a block item from the mast's input slot, such as a seed or a sapling, in every empty cell it can stand in. It plants wherever the item can survive, wanted or not.
feedback.jei.info.pivot_tip_feed: Uses the item in the mast's input slot on whatever is in each cell: feed on an animal, bone meal on a crop, shears on a sheep. It does not choose; a wrong item is spent as readily as a right one.
feedback.jei.info.pivot_tip_strike: Strikes creatures in the cells it crosses, with the weight of the seated machine head. Hurts anything living, including a player.
feedback.jei.info.pivot_tip_collect: Sweeps dropped items into the mast's output slots, which a hopper or belt can empty.
feedback.jei.info.dark_cell: The controller of a mob farm, set in the wall of a sealed room. The room is the cell: if it is closed and dark inside, hostile mobs gather there as a count, not as creatures, up to the room's capacity. Kill-method blocks set in the wall (fall, fire, crush, fume, shock, radiation) work on what has gathered, and the drops come out of the cell into a chest, hopper or belt beside the controller. Mobs the walls do not hold back wear the shield down once the room is crowded; mend it by hand with building blocks. At nothing left, the mobs spill out. A Catalyst Tap in reach takes the XP of zombies and skeletons at a loss. Empty hand reads the cell.
feedback.jei.info.fall_plate: A kill method for the wall of a dark cell. Drops what stands on it; the height (small, medium, large) is stepped with an empty hand. Harms only mobs that take fall damage.
feedback.jei.info.fire_plate: A kill method for the wall of a dark cell. Burns what stands on it, as hot as the heat pointed at it. Mobs that do not burn are untouched. Food drops come out cooked; left in the output, food chars.
feedback.jei.info.crush_head: A kill method for the wall of a dark cell. A hammer on a vertical shaft: put a machine head in it and turn it. Its harm is the head's strength; a head too light for the mobs wears.
feedback.jei.info.fume_port: A kill method for the wall of a dark cell. Takes a toxic gas by pipe or bucket and lets it into the room. Harms only mobs that breathe; the worse the gas, the worse the harm. A full tank with nothing to do seeps into the room outside.
feedback.jei.info.shock_plate: A kill method for the wall of a dark cell. Passes the current it is given through what stands on it. Big bodies are scorched, so their drops are charred. A few mobs shrug off a shock.
feedback.jei.info.radiation_source: A kill method for the wall of a dark cell. Holds one radioactive item and kills everything alive in the room with it. The drops come out contaminated and give off radiation themselves, and so does the source: stand clear.
feedback.darkcell.report: Cell of %s blocks, %s mobs, shield %s%%, %s kill methods
feedback.jei.info.stoker: A screw feed that pushes solid fuel into the firebox in front of it, driven by a vertical shaft. Three drum sizes, stepped with an empty hand, set how much each turn moves. A hopper or belt fills it from any side but the front. It does not look at the fire: a full firebox refuses the fuel and the feed stalls.
feedback.jei.info.creel: A basket trap for water. Set it where it is under water in a pond, river or sea; a puddle catches nothing. Every couple of minutes it draws a catch from the same fish and junk the water gives a rod, never treasure; bait in the top slot shortens the wait and is spent. An empty hand empties the basket, and a hopper can take from it. A full basket stops.
feedback.jei.info.fish_wheel: A water wheel with baskets on its blades. It turns in a current like any wheel but gives half the power, and while it turns it draws a catch from the same fish the water gives a rod, never treasure; more blades in the current catch faster. An empty hand empties the baskets, and a hopper can take from them. A full basket stops the catch, not the wheel.
feedback.jei.info.kiln_zone: A tunnel kiln zone. Ware goes in at the back from a hopper or belt, rides a car through four positions of heat (a cool start, two hot, a cool finish) and comes out the front into whatever takes items. Heat comes from a firebox or burner pointed at it; the car is driven by a vertical shaft, and its speed sets how long ware stays: slow gives a clean result, fast leaves ware raw, a stopped car leaves it in the fire to char, crack or spoil. It runs food by its cooking ladder and anything else by the same rows a furnace uses, but does not melt metal.
gui.feedback.depot.linked: Linked. Parcels on the road here: %s
gui.feedback.depot.unlinked: Not linked: use a link card on this and another depot.
feedback.depot.recorded: Depot recorded on the card. Use it on another depot to link them.
feedback.depot.same: That is the depot already recorded.
feedback.depot.unreachable: The recorded depot is gone or too far to reach: the card keeps what it recorded.
feedback.jei.info.depot: One end of a trade road. Link it to a depot in another village with a link card, put goods on the outgoing shelf, and lay a road (path, gravel, stone, brick or planks) leaving it. On the next market day a convoy carries the outgoing goods to the other depot, which carries its own to yours; the trip takes longer the farther apart the depots are. Raiders take some stacks on the road, fewer when a bell stands near either end. A donkey courier is seen setting out when a player is there. The incoming shelf is taken from, not put on. Villages pay differently for the same goods: carry what the other village wants.
feedback.jei.info.depot_link_card: Use it on a depot to record that depot, then on another depot to link the two. The link is wiped from the card when made.
village.feedback.cross.inactive: This square is too small or not paved: the cross needs a wide, open, paved square.
village.feedback.cross.today: Market day. The trader is in.
village.feedback.cross.in: The next market is in %s days.
village.feedback.board.raid: A raid is on. Stocked shelves draw raiders: guard them.
village.feedback.board.bounty: A banner bounty stands: %s emeralds for an illager banner (%s owed). Put one in the slot on the Contracts tab and press Banner.
village.feedback.board.market_none: No market square stands near the board.
village.feedback.board.market_today: Market day today at the cross.
feedback.jei.info.market_cross: A pillar for a paved square. Pave a wide, open square (path, gravel, stone, brick or planks, with sky above) and set the cross on it: when the square is big enough the cross is active, and every eighth day the wandering trader sets up at it for the day. Villagers near an active cross want more things and make another errand that day, and shops near it restock. A village that honours you brings a second trader selling goods of its region. Right-click it to read whether the square counts and when the next market is.
gui.feedback.board.no_orders: No villager in range has an order.
gui.feedback.board.no_contracts: The village has posted no contracts.
village.feedback.board.contract_line: %s of %s delivered, at least %s, %s days left, %s each
village.feedback.board.standing.0: The village does not know you.
village.feedback.board.next.1: Next: yet more contracts each day, and a bigger bonus for finishing.
village.feedback.board.next.2: Next: honoured standing earns a blueprint for every contract finished.
feedback.jei.info.ledger_board: The village's notice board. Place it near the bell. Right-click it to read, in one place, every open order of the villagers around it grouped by what is asked, the contracts the village has posted, and the notices. A contract asks several pieces of one kind, each at least Good; put a piece in the slot and deliver it, or let a Counter within twelve blocks of the board fill contracts from what reaches it. Each piece pays by its class, and finishing a contract adds a bonus and raises the village's regard of you; an Exceptional run, or an honoured village, earns a blueprint. The board stores nothing about a player: it reads the villagers' own gossip.
feedback.counter.catchment: In reach %s, want something here %s, errands pending %s, out of reach %s. Today: walk-in sales %s, hand-over sales %s.
gui.feedback.counter.hint: Click to buy one, Shift-click a stack. Prices are emeralds each.
feedback.jei.info.counter: A shop counter with a nine-slot shelf. The front is the customer side: right-click the front or top to buy from the shelf with emeralds, which go into the till. The back is the keeper side: stock the shelf, set a price on each slot and take the till. A stocked shelf draws villagers: one that is idle or meeting, has no errand left to run and wants something on the shelf, and has a way to walk to the front, comes and buys at your price. A villager sealed in a cell has no way and never comes. Roads of path, gravel, stone or planks carry the reach farther down the street. A villager buys above market up to a ceiling, and gossips against the keeper for it. Hand-over still works: goods fed into the intake from the sides are handed to a villager within 8 blocks as a delivery would be, and a want sold this way pays three quarters of its line. Emeralds come out of the till slots and whatever was not taken comes out of the returns. Hoppers fill the shelf from the back and top. Right-click a side to read the catchment.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.textured: A broad belt with a ribbed face. Grips better.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.link: Linked plates. Grips less and takes far more heat.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.pack: A big pack: 27 slots, and it weighs on the wearer.
modular.feedback.role.bowl.tip: The scoop. Its material sets how much it holds and how it takes heat.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.gun_buffer: A hydraulic buffer behind the bolt: it slows the cycle a little and takes much of the kick.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.gun_obturato: A seal that stops gas slipping past the round: less kick and tighter spread, until it burns through.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.gun_reticle: A lit sight picture: tighter spread, visible only in low light.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.gun_sear: A magnet holds the sear: tighter spread and a slightly quicker cycle.
modular.feedback.fig.mass.tip.cell: What the stack weighs. Swung as a club it hits harder for it; the charge it holds does not change.
modular.feedback.fig.mass.tip.charge: What the charge weighs, filler and casing.
modular.feedback.fig.mass.tip.gun: What the gun weighs unloaded. A heavier gun kicks less and swings slower as a bludgeon.
modular.feedback.fig.mass.tip.shield: Every part's volume times its material's density. A heavier shield swings and raises slower.
commands.feedback.blueprint: Gave a blueprint of the held item.
commands.feedback.no_modular: Hold a modular item (not a blueprint).
advancement.feedback.combat.this_is_very: Fire an assault rifle with a pistol grip.
advancement.feedback.combat.big_iron.des: A big iron on your hip: fire a revolver with the longest barrel there is.
advancement.feedback.combat.long_ass_gun: A Gun, of the Long-Ass Variety
I shot Darnell with a long-ass gun then tossed it in the aquarium!
gui.feedback.blueprint_table.conflict: Cannot go on with what is fitted now.
modular.feedback.desc.part.engine_block: The block the cylinders are bored in. Its layout sets how the engine runs: inline is plain, a V is compact and light but revs lower, a boxer is heavier and revs higher.
modular.feedback.desc.part.piston_set: The pistons, one per cylinder. Their count is the cylinders; their metal sets how fast they may move, and so the redline.
modular.feedback.desc.part.crankshaft: Turns the pistons' stroke into rotation. A forged crank revs higher than a cast one; a crank of a weaker metal than the pistons holds the revs down.
modular.feedback.desc.part.cylinder_head: Closes the cylinders. Its compression ratio decides which fuels it runs well on: low misfires on nothing and knocks on nothing, high makes more torque and knocks on low-ignition fuel.
modular.feedback.desc.part.gear_set: The gear wheels of a gearbox. Their count is the number of forward gears; their metal sets how fast a shift at speed wears them.
modular.feedback.desc.part.synchro_ring: Matches the speed of a gear to the shaft before it engages.
modular.feedback.desc.part.gearbox_case: Holds the gears and what keeps them oiled.
modular.feedback.role.engine_block.tip: The engine block. Its layout sets torque per liter, how high the engine revs and how heavy it is.
modular.feedback.role.pistons.tip: The pistons. Their shape is the number of cylinders, the bore you set is their width, and their metal is the engine's: it must be a metal with a measured yield strength, and sets the redline.
modular.feedback.role.crankshaft.tip: The crank. The stroke you set is how far a piston travels: a short stroke revs higher, a long one makes more torque. A cast crank revs lower than a forged one.
modular.feedback.role.cylinder_head.tip: The head. Its compression ratio sets which fuels the engine runs well on, and a little of its torque.
modular.feedback.role.gear_set.tip: The gears. Their shape is how many forward gears there are, and you set the ratio of each: input turns per output turn, so 3.5 is a low gear and 0.8 an overdrive. Their metal sets how fast a shift at speed wears the box.
modular.feedback.role.synchro.tip: A dog clutch is plain and wears the box most when shifted at speed; a synchromesh matches speeds first and wears it far less, for a little weight.
modular.feedback.role.gearbox_case.tip: The case. Dry, splash or pressure oiling: the more oil reaches the gears, the less a shift at speed wears them and the heavier the case.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.inline_blo: Cylinders in a row: the plain layout.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.v_block: Two banks at an angle: a short, light block that revs a little lower.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.boxer_bloc: Opposed banks that cancel each other's shake: revs higher, but a heavier block with a touch less torque.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.six_cylind: Six cylinders: twice the swept volume of three, and the ingots to match.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.eight_cyli: Eight cylinders: the most torque, and the most metal.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.cast_crank: A poured crank: cheap, but it will not rev as high.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.forged_cra: A hammered crank: stronger, so the engine revs higher, for more metal.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.low_compre: Runs on fuels that ignite easily without knocking, and makes a little less torque.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.high_compr: More torque, but a fuel that ignites easily knocks and wears the engine.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.six_speed: Six forward gears: the widest spread, and the most metal.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.dog_clutch: Plain dogs that mesh as they are: a shift at speed wears the box.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.synchromes: Rings that match the gear's speed before it meshes: a shift at speed wears the box about two fifths less.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.dry_case: Grease only: the lightest case, and the gears wear most.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.splash_cas: The gears dip in an oil bath: a quarter less wear on shifts.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.pressure_c: An oil pump feeds the gears: half the wear, and the heaviest case.
feedback.jei.info.engine: A piston engine: block, pistons, crank and head, built at a Smithing Table from a blueprint drawn at the Blueprint Table, where you also set the bore and stroke. Place it against the end of a shaft; it burns fuel from its own tank and turns the shaft like a Steam Engine.
modular.feedback.desc.part.vessel_shell: The wall of a pressure vessel. Its shape and thickness, and its metal's strength, set the pressure it holds and the room inside.
modular.feedback.role.vessel_shell.tip: The shell. A thicker wall holds more pressure and leaves less room. A sphere carries a load best, a flat box worst but fills the block. Its metal needs a measured yield strength.
modular.feedback.desc.part.exchanger_cor: The tubes of a heat exchanger. Their metal's conductivity and the area they present set how fast heat crosses.
modular.feedback.role.exchanger_core.tip: The tubes. A metal that conducts heat well and more area move heat faster. The metal needs a stated conductivity.
modular.feedback.desc.part.tank_shell: The wall of a gas tank. Its shape and thickness, and its metal's strength, set the pressure it holds and the room inside.
modular.feedback.role.tank_shell.tip: The shell. A thicker wall holds more pressure and leaves less room. A sphere carries a load best, a flat box worst but holds most. Its metal needs a measured yield strength.
modular.feedback.desc.part.wheel_rim: The rim and buckets of a water wheel. Its size and bucket count set the power it makes and how slowly it turns; its wood sets its momentum.
modular.feedback.role.wheel_rim.tip: The rim. A bigger wheel and more buckets give more power; a bigger wheel turns slower for the same flow; a heavier rim holds more momentum.
modular.feedback.desc.part.store_core: The wall of a thermal store. A thick wall has more to heat and loses less; its material's conductivity sets the loss.
modular.feedback.role.store_core.tip: The wall. Thicker holds heat longer and takes longer to charge. Ceramic keeps heat; metal gives it away.
modular.feedback.desc.part.jar_glass: The glass of a Leyden jar. More plate area holds more charge, thinner glass more again, and thinner glass leaks it faster.
modular.feedback.role.jar_glass.tip: The glass. It must insulate. Thin glass stores more and leaks much faster; more area stores more.
Hoop bands round the shell. A strong band metal against the shell's raises the pressure it carries.
modular.feedback.role.relief_valve.tip: A valve that opens near the danger line and lets air out, so a pump that outruns the leak still cannot burst it.
modular.feedback.role.fin_stack.tip: A second metal bonded to the tubes. Its conductivity adds to the heat that crosses.
modular.feedback.role.rim_ring.tip: A ring of dense metal round the rim. More momentum, and slower to spin up.
modular.feedback.role.lagging.tip: A poor conductor wrapped round the outside. The poorer, the less heat the store loses.
modular.feedback.role.salt_fill.tip: Salt packed inside: more stuff to heat, so the store holds more.
modular.feedback.role.foil.tip: Foil lining the jar. The more current its metal carries, the harder the jar discharges.
modular.feedback.role.outer_sleeve.tip: A glass sleeve over the jar. A second insulator: the charge leaks away more slowly.
modular.feedback.desc.part.pump_impeller: The impeller of a pump. Its diameter and shape set how much it moves and how hard it is to turn.
modular.feedback.role.pump_impeller.tip: The impeller. A bigger one moves more and is harder to turn. Axial moves the most and lifts poorly; a screw moves little and lifts well.
modular.feedback.role.volute.tip: A casing that turns speed into flow: a pump moves a little more for a little more load.
modular.feedback.desc.part.compressor_ro: The rotor of a compressor. Its size and staging set how much it moves, how hard it is to turn, and how hot it heats the gas.
modular.feedback.role.compressor_rotor.t: The rotor. A bigger one moves more and is harder to turn. Staging moves more and heats the gas less, at more load.
modular.feedback.role.intercooler.tip: Takes heat out of the gas between stages, so it leaves cooler.
modular.feedback.desc.part.thruster_nozz: The nozzle of a thruster. Its bore sets how hard it pushes and how much fuel it burns; its shape trades push against fuel.
modular.feedback.role.thruster_nozzle.ti: The nozzle. A wider bore pushes harder and burns more fuel. A cone pushes hardest and burns most; a throat pushes least and sips fuel.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.nozzle_bel: A bell that expands the jet: the baseline push and the baseline burn.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.nozzle_con: A wide cone: pushes 30% harder, and burns 50% more fuel.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.nozzle_thr: A bare throat: pushes 30% less, and burns half the fuel.
modular.feedback.role.regen_jacket.tip: A plate wrapped round the nozzle that the fuel runs through first. The fuel arrives warm, so 15% less of it burns for the same push.
feedback.jei.info.thruster: Pushes the body it is part of along its facing, burning liquid fuel from a pipe or bucket; right-click to switch it on. It needs air to burn (not in the End, not underwater) unless the fuel carries its own oxygen. Built at a Smithing Table from a blueprint drawn at the Blueprint Table (Aerospace Treatise II): the nozzle's bore and shape set the push and the fuel it burns, a regen jacket saves fuel.
modular.feedback.desc.part.burner_nozzle: The nozzle of a burner. Its bore sets how much fuel it burns; its shape trades burn against flame temperature.
modular.feedback.role.burner_nozzle.tip: The nozzle. A wider bore burns more fuel. A jet burns more and hotter; a wick burns little and cooler.
modular.feedback.role.flame_holder.tip: A small metal piece that steadies the flame, which burns a little hotter.
modular.feedback.desc.part.crank_arm: The arm of a hand crank. A long arm is more lever and a slower hand.
modular.feedback.role.crank_arm.tip: The arm. Longer is more Su and fewer RPM. An offset crank has more lever for a little less speed.
modular.feedback.role.crank_flywheel.tip: A small disc on the crank: it carries the turn through the dead spot, and is slower to start.
modular.feedback.desc.part.magnet_core: The core of an electromagnet. More turns pull harder and draw more current; the shape trades pull against reach.
modular.feedback.role.magnet_core.tip: The core. More turns pull harder and draw more current. A horseshoe pulls harder and reaches less; a pot core pulls hardest and barely reaches.
modular.feedback.role.yoke.tip: Closes the magnetic path: a little more pull for the same current.
modular.feedback.desc.part.cell_anode: The anode of a galvanic cell. A bigger one feeds more current and lasts longer; the shape trades current against life.
modular.feedback.role.cell_anode.tip: The anode. A bigger one gives more current and lasts longer. A plate gives more current for a shorter life; a block lasts longest.
modular.feedback.role.copper_cathode.tip: A copper plate in the cell: a little more current.
modular.feedback.desc.part.lamp_filament: The filament of a lamp. A thicker one draws more current and lasts longer.
modular.feedback.role.lamp_filament.tip: The filament, which must conduct. Thicker draws more and lasts longer. Carbon draws more and is tougher; a fine one draws little and burns out sooner.
modular.feedback.role.ballast.tip: A small resistor in line: the lamp rides a little overvoltage before it burns out.
figure.feedback.block.Burnout: Burns out at %s times rated volts
modular.feedback.desc.part.boiler_shell: The shell of a boiler. Its wall, shape and metal set the pressure it risks letting go at; the valve and seams follow it.
modular.feedback.role.boiler_shell.tip: The shell. A thicker wall holds more pressure. A water-tube shell carries more than a fire-tube one; a flat box least. Its metal needs a measured yield strength.
modular.feedback.desc.part.large_boiler_: The shell of a boiler. Its wall, shape and metal set the pressure it risks letting go at; the valve and seams follow it.
modular.feedback.role.large_boiler_shell: The shell. A thicker wall holds more pressure. A water-tube shell carries more than a fire-tube one; a flat box least. Its metal needs a measured yield strength.
modular.feedback.desc.part.flywheel_disc: The disc of a flywheel. Radius and thickness set its momentum; its metal's strength over its weight sets how fast it can spin before the rim strains.
modular.feedback.role.flywheel_disc.tip: The disc. Momentum rises steeply with radius, but a bigger disc strains at fewer RPM. Dense metal holds more momentum; strong, light metal spins faster.
modular.feedback.role.rim_band.tip: Hoop bands round the rim. A strong band metal lets the disc spin faster before the rim strains.
modular.feedback.role.flywheel_bearing.t: A better bearing: less drag for carrying the disc.
modular.feedback.desc.part.prop_hub: The centre the blades bolt to. Its shape is the number of blades.
modular.feedback.desc.part.prop_blades: The blades. Their pitch and diameter set the thrust and the speed it pulls to, and their metal sets the tip speed they survive.
modular.feedback.role.prop_hub.tip: The hub. Its shape is the number of blades: more blades pull harder for the same diameter and weigh more.
modular.feedback.role.prop_blades.tip: The blades. The diameter you set is the disc they sweep; pitch is their angle. Their metal, which needs a measured yield strength, sets the tip speed they survive.
feedback.jei.info.gas_cell: One cell of an airship's envelope. It holds a lift gas (hydrogen, wisp gas or helium) from a pipe or bucket, and cells that touch share it. The air it pushes aside weighs more than the gas, and the difference lifts the cell where it sits, so how a ship is loaded decides how it trims; thin air at height lifts less. A cell stretches as the air thins: climb with a full cell past what its skin takes and it weeps gas until a Vent Valve lets some out first. An arrow or bullet leaves a hole that leaks until you patch it by hand with cloth, rubber or a plate. Hydrogen and wisp gas burn, and a flame, lava or a running thruster beside a cell lights the whole envelope; helium never does. Cloth and rubber skins burn away with their gas.
feedback.jei.info.vent_valve: Lets gas out of the gas cells beside it, to come down or to relieve a full cell on the climb. Use it to open or shut it by hand, or set it from a Controller card.
feedback.jei.info.ballast_tank: A tank of water that weighs the craft down. Fill it with a bucket or a pipe; use it to dump the water by hand, or set the dump from a Controller card. Dumping lightens the craft, so it rises.
feedback.jei.info.propeller: An aircraft propeller: hub and blades, built at a Smithing Table from a blueprint drawn at the Blueprint Table, where you also set the diameter. Place it on the end of a shaft; it pulls the vehicle when turned, and tears itself apart if its tips are driven faster than the metal holds.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.two_blade: Two blades: light and cheap, and the least thrust for the disc.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.four_blade: Four blades: more thrust for the same diameter, and heavier.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.fine_pitch: Shallow blade angle: a climb prop, strong at low airspeed and soon out of bite at speed.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.medium_pit: Middling blade angle: a fair thrust and top speed.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.coarse_pit: Steep blade angle: a cruise prop, weak at low airspeed and fast once moving.
feedback.jei.info.transmission: A gearbox: gear set, synchro and case, built at a Smithing Table from a blueprint drawn at the Blueprint Table, where you set the ratio of each gear. Place it in a drivetrain; a shifter picks neutral, a forward gear or reverse.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.smoothbore: A plain tube, one cell of stock. A chamber gun's barrel: the round is thrown by burning charge. Bullets scatter more than from a rifled bore.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.rifled: Two cells of stock, cut with spiral grooves that spin the bullet. A chamber gun's barrel; a single bullet flies much truer than from a smoothbore.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.gun_rifling: Spiral grooves spin the bullet: its spread is %1$s%% of a plain bore's.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.long_gun: A longer receiver for a long barrel to steady the bullet. It takes a stock to brace against the shoulder. What it is called follows from the barrel: rifled and narrow a rifle, smooth and wide a shotgun, smooth and narrow a musket, rifled and wide a slug gun.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.flintlock: A hammer holding a flint, over a pan of priming powder. Slow to prime and cock between shots, and about one pull in eight flashes in the pan without firing.
advancement.feedback.progress.root.title: Technology
advancement.feedback.progress.root.descr: Stone and wood tools, and no fire you control. Everything starts there.
advancement.feedback.progress.combat_roo: Guns, blades and the skills that make you good with them.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.first: Stone and wood only. Make a fire that stays where you put it.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.reada: A fire has a temperature, and a number beats a guess. Find something that reads it.
Copper melts in a fire you can build. Find a vessel that holds the melt.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.bronz: Copper alone is soft. Mix it with something.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.iron_: Iron wants a hotter fire that also strips the oxygen from the ore. Push more air, hold more heat.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.steel: Iron with a little carbon, melted clean.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.tempe: Fresh steel is brittle or soft. Heat and cooling decide which.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.hard_: Steel fails at heat and wear. Press and sinter something harder.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.hotte: A fuel fire tops out and makes smoke. Find a heat that does not.
advancement.feedback.progress.rotation.c: All of this is hand work and your arm is the only power. Turn it into a shaft.
advancement.feedback.progress.rotation.w: A crank needs a person. A river does not.
advancement.feedback.progress.rotation.s: Rivers stay put. Make a shaft turn on fire, anywhere.
Hand-made parts are loose and rough. Make a machine cut to size.
advancement.feedback.progress.rotation.e: Steam is heavy for its power. Burn something refined inside the machine.
advancement.feedback.progress.electricit: Rub something and hear it snap. Make it repeatable.
Two metals and a wet gap. A steady push with nothing moving.
A shaft only carries work as far as the gears go. Turn rotation into something that travels.
Run a wire to a machine no shaft can reach.
advancement.feedback.progress.control.ti: Machines run until told to stop, and the output suffers. Make one stop on its own.
advancement.feedback.progress.control.co: Reflexes are fixed. Build something you can tell what to do, then give it something to read.
advancement.feedback.progress.control.me: One program fills a controller. Store more than it holds.
Plain rock and water hide a lot. Start with salt.
advancement.feedback.progress.chem.elect: Drive current through water or brine and see what comes apart.
Metals will not dissolve in water. A reactor and an acid might.
advancement.feedback.progress.chem.oil.d: Fuel is wood and coal. The ground has more.
advancement.feedback.progress.chem.press: Some reactions only go when squeezed. Contain it, and leave it a way out.
advancement.feedback.progress.chem.alumi: Some ores will not smelt. Electricity can reduce them.
Cooking is hand work too. Find a table to prepare things on.
advancement.feedback.progress.food.skill: Heat a pan and watch it. Food does not wait for you.
advancement.feedback.progress.food.pot.d: Some food wants hours and more than one ingredient.
advancement.feedback.progress.combat.arm: Powder, a barrel and a steady hand. Shape its parts at a Smithing Table, Woodworking Table or Stonecutter and assemble a gun at the Engineering Table.
advancement.feedback.progress.nether.net: What the Nether gives is not yet usable. Melt it down and cast it.
advancement.feedback.progress.deepdark.x: Experience can be held, if you find something to hold it.
advancement.feedback.progress.deepdark.e: Write an effect in a script that is not yours.
Some rocks give off more than heat. Find a way to hear it.
A heat source is only a heat source. Make one that sustains itself, and keep it cooled.
advancement.feedback.progress.ender.port: The End is out of reach by hand. Send something there anyway.
advancement.feedback.progress.vehicles.s: An engine on a stand goes nowhere. Sit on something that does.
advancement.feedback.combat.dodge_this.d: Shoot an Enderman with a bullet. It dodges arrows, not this.
advancement.feedback.combat.newton_was_r: Fire until the recoil throws you, or the gun.
advancement.feedback.combat.remember_rem: Fire a flintlock. Treason and plot optional.
advancement.feedback.progress.joke.press: Let a boiler find out where the pressure goes.
advancement.feedback.progress.joke.told_: Let an overspeed trip save a shaft from itself.
advancement.feedback.progress.joke.skill: Feed a machine more force than the work can take, and wear it.
advancement.feedback.progress.joke.hot_t: Meet something hot with your bare skin.
advancement.feedback.progress.joke.aw_ma: Carry a creeper charge into a fire, a fall or an explosion.
Put a phosphor screen on it. Surely.
feedback.jei.info.converter: Steps a line's voltage by a named ratio: divide by 4, divide by 16 or multiply by 4 (click it with an empty hand to pick). Wire the line you step from to the converter and set a Converter Tap against it; the tap is where the stepped line starts, and the two never share a run. Nearly all the power comes out, but the loss is heat in the block: set aluminium Heatsinks against it, because a hot converter loses condition and wastes more. It passes a fixed amount of power, so a lower voltage out is more amps.
feedback.jei.info.converter_tap: The output side of a Solid-State Converter. Set it against the converter; wire the line you step to onto the tap. Alone it supplies nothing.
feedback.jei.info.heatsink: Finned aluminium. Set against a Solid-State Converter (up to four), it sheds the converter's heat to the air faster.
feedback.jei.info.thermal_store: A tank that holds heat, not electricity, built at a Stonecutter from a blueprint drawn at the Blueprint Table. A thick wall has more to heat, so it charges slowly, but it loses less; a thin one charges fast and cools fast. The wall's own conductivity sets the loss, so ceramic keeps heat and metal gives it away. Optional addons: a lagging of poorly conducting stuff cuts the loss, and a salt fill adds heat mass.
message.feedback.tuned_eye.tuned: The eye tunes to this pair.
message.feedback.tuned_eye.untuned: The eye points nowhere. Use it on a port first.
message.feedback.tuned_eye.none: The other end is not placed anywhere.
message.feedback.tuned_eye.elsewhere: The other end is in another dimension.
feedback.jei.info.tuned_eye: A pearl tuned to a bonded pair. Use it on a port to tune it; use it in the air to read how far the other end is and which way, even when that end is far away or unloaded. Crafted from a pearl and redstone dust.
feedback.jei.info.synthetic_pearl: Pressed from silica glass, redstone chromium and teleportant at high heat. It does everything a pearl does: it makes a bonded pair, tunes an eye and blinks. Endermen drop real pearls the cheap way.
feedback.jei.info.porous_aggregate: What end stone leaves after its trapped hydrogen is driven off in a Reactor: a porous, very light rock that barely conducts heat.
gui.feedback.reloading_press.idle: Seat a case and a charge to read the round.
message.feedback.disenchant_stone: An attunement ground off the part.
feedback.jei.info.orb_absorber: Pulls loose experience orbs within a few blocks into the XP wire it sits on, once a second. What the run cannot hold stays in the world as orbs.
feedback.jei.info.ore_tap: Takes the experience of ore (or any block that pays it) broken within eight blocks into its XP run. Mining machines pay XP the same as a pickaxe.
feedback.jei.info.trade_tap: Takes the experience a villager trade pays, when the villager is within eight blocks, into its XP run. A Counter sale or purchase pays it too, only into a tap: no orbs drop.
feedback.jei.info.smelter_tap: Drains the experience a vessel beside it banked from cooking recipes into its XP run, twenty points a second. A vessel with no tap holds its bank until broken, then spills it as orbs.
feedback.jei.info.disenchant_stone: Right-click with an attuned part: one attunement is ground off, and half of what the session cost comes back as XP into a run beside the stone, or as orbs if there is none.
feedback.jei.info.crystal_holder: Seats one XP container (an XP container tool or a Reservoir-attuned tool) and shows its store on the XP wire next to it. Take the stack out to take its XP.
feedback.jei.info.coolant_port: A wall cell of the reactor shell. Water goes in by pipe or bucket; the core feeds it to its coolant channels, and the steam they make comes out the same block. With no water the channels carry nothing away and the core climbs.
feedback.jei.info.coolant_channel: A lattice cell that carries heat off the core as water boiling to steam in the Coolant Port. The water slows neutrons a little for the fuel cells beside it, so a channel run dry costs the core some reactivity.
feedback.jei.info.neutron_reflector: A shell wall cell that sends neutrons back into the fuel cells it touches, raising their multiplication. Counts as a sound wall.
feedback.jei.info.star_seat: A lattice cell that seats one Nether star. The star is never used up: it adds reactivity to every live fuel cell, delays the core's temperature feedback, and holds a core with no fuel at a low idle.
feedback.jei.info.flux_meter: Reads a reactor core's neutron flux as a fraction of full power. Use it on the core.
feedback.jei.info.spent_fuel_pool: Holds up to nine spent fuel rods under water. A freshly discharged rod keeps making decay heat for days; the water takes it, boiling away over 100 Tu, so keep the pool topped up. A pool run dry heats its rods until they slump into radioactive slag, and gives off a dose while it is dry. Put a rod in with the rod in hand, fill with a bucket, sneak with an empty hand to take one out.
feedback.jei.info.gas_centrifuge: Put it on a shaft. Natural uranium ingots go in by hand (four to a batch), hydrofluoric acid by bucket or pipe (50 mB a batch). Above 24 RPM it spins out a batch: one Enriched Uranium ingot and three Depleted Uranium ingots, faster the faster the shaft turns (by the square). Right-click with an empty hand to take what it made, or to read it.
feedback.jei.info.enriched_fuel_rod: Enriched uranium clad in stainless steel: much stronger than a natural Fuel Rod, so a core runs hotter on fewer rods.
feedback.jei.info.breeder_rod: Depleted uranium around thorium. It breeds fissile fuel fast, but only in a hard spectrum: put it where no moderator or flowing coolant touches it.
gui.feedback.computer.app_hint: Runs while this disk is in a drive.
feedback.programmer.erased: Erased. The program is back in the editor.
feedback.programmer.function_bad: That selection cannot be saved as a function.
feedback.jei.info.circuit_board: A Controller's mid-game program medium: written once at a Programmer like a Punch Card, to be thrown away and replaced rather than rewritten.
feedback.jei.info.floppy_disk: A program medium you can rewrite. Put a printed disk in a Programmer and press Erase: the program comes back into the editor, and Print writes the new one onto the same disk. A Floppy Disk crafted with an item (a spyglass for Scope, a compass for Link Map, a book for Notes, a clock for Converter, redstone for Calculator, a bookshelf for Library, a redstone lamp for Power, a note block for Arcade, paper and blue dye for Blueprint) becomes an app disk: its app runs on a Computer while the disk is in one of its drives.
feedback.jei.info.usb_drive: A program medium you can rewrite, like a Floppy Disk. Any Controller takes it where it takes a Punch Card.
feedback.jei.info.function_card: Saves a selection of cards from a Programmer. Hold a blank one, select cards, press Save fn. Hold a saved one and press Stamp to drop its cards into the editor as plain cards with their inputs unwired; Print flattens them into the program. Needs no Controller support: a function is a convenience, not a new kind of card.
feedback.controller.wrong_medium: This block does not take that medium.
feedback.jei.info.electric_controller: A Controller powered from a cable, not a shaft. It takes every program medium: Punch Card, Circuit Board, Floppy Disk and USB Drive. It runs while the line delivers at least half of what it wants.
feedback.jei.info.electric_programmer: A Programmer that takes every program medium. The mechanical Programmer takes the Punch Card only. Erase works on a printed Floppy Disk or USB Drive.
feedback.jei.info.computer: An Electric Programmer and an Electric Controller in one block. Right-click for its desktop: four drive bays and a running slot are icons you drag media onto, your hotbar sits in a dock, widgets show the time, a scope of the running program's first sensor and each drive's memory, and the apps open as windows from the Menu or the icons. Open a drive to Edit it (the node editor opens in its own resizable window), Run it or Eject it; the Monitor shows the running program's variables and sensor readings, Links lists the blocks its cards are linked to, and Settings changes the phosphor colour, wallpaper, screen effects and widgets, which are kept on the block. Sneak with an empty hand to take the running medium out. The editor works without power; the program runs only while the cable delivers.
gui.feedback.computer.editor_empty: Nothing is open. Pick a drive, then Edit.
gui.feedback.computer.files.hint: Drag a program onto another drive to copy it onto a blank Floppy or USB drive, or onto the trash to erase it. Right-click a drive for more.
gui.feedback.computer.files.hint_plain: Copying and dragging need the Library disk. Right-click a drive for its menu.
gui.feedback.computer.no_blank_there: %s: is not a blank Floppy or USB drive.
gui.feedback.computer.notes_hint: Type here. Saved on this Computer.
gui.feedback.computer.group.metal.note: One Qu is a nugget. Molten metal is 16 mB per Qu.
gui.feedback.computer.group.volume.note: 1 mB is a litre. 1000 mB fills a block.
gui.feedback.computer.group.time.note: 20 ticks to the second, 24000 to a day.
gui.feedback.computer.copy_note: Copy needs a blank Floppy or USB drive, alone in another bay.
gui.feedback.computer.no_blank: No blank Floppy or USB drive in another bay.
gui.feedback.computer.icons_note: Icon side applies when the desktop is opened again.
gui.feedback.computer.no_links: The running program has no linked cards.
gui.feedback.enchant.unknown_tip: You do not know this effect. Attempt it blind (no guide on the pad, full price), study a part that already has it, or read a book.
message.feedback.book.known: You already know what this book teaches.
advancement.feedback.progress.combat.siz: Look a creature over until it gives something away.
advancement.feedback.progress.combat.exp: Spend a read on one large blow and land it.
advancement.feedback.progress.combat.sof: Pick the worn piece under your crosshair and strike through it.
advancement.feedback.progress.combat.rea: Watch a creature take aim at you, and be somewhere else when it lets go.
advancement.feedback.progress.combat.wro: Hit armour with something softer than it. It will not go well.
advancement.feedback.progress.combat.rig: Hit armour with a weapon harder than what it wears, and let it show.
advancement.feedback.progress.combat.hot: Finish a fight with a blade or barrel whose edge runs hot.
advancement.feedback.progress.combat.spe: Land a hit with a spear while the use key is held.
advancement.feedback.progress.combat.arm: Be hit while wearing armour you built, and take less for it.
Take a blow wearing a full outfit of armour you built.
advancement.feedback.progress.combat.fir: Cast a technique from any skill tree.
advancement.feedback.progress.combat.cas: Use a technique from the Anchor tree. Stand your ground.
Use a technique from the Veil tree. Be elsewhere.
Use a technique from the Brute tree. Put your weight in it.
Use a technique from the Onslaught tree. Keep the rhythm.
Use a technique from the Observation tree. Read first, then act.
Use a technique from the Proficiency tree. Get out of trouble.
Use a technique from the Chaos tree. Leave them with what you did.
advancement.feedback.combat.overrun.desc: Fire a round the chamber was never built to hold.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.tongs: Lift or carry something too hot for bare skin, with tongs or gloves between you and it.
advancement.feedback.progress.hazard.ste: Stand in the steam a weeping boiler seam gives off, and live. The sound comes before the pain.
advancement.feedback.progress.hazard.bac: Bring a boiler that has started to weep back under its seam line before it lets go.
advancement.feedback.progress.hazard.rad: Carry a counter or dosimeter through a dose sick enough to make you hungry, and come out the other side.
advancement.feedback.progress.joke.overd: Leave a batch in the heat long past done. It is done.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.tin.d: Some metal melts in a cooler fire than copper and stays bright. Find it in the ground.
A dense grey ore melts at a fire you can already build. It is soft, and it is poison to handle carelessly.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.brass: Copper takes a second metal and turns the colour of gold. Not tin this time.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.glass: Sand melts, if the fire is hot and the vessel holds. What it gives is clear.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.quart: Plain glass softens early. Pure silica holds its shape much hotter, and wants a much hotter fire.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.fireb: Ordinary brick cracks in a hot fire. A particular clay, fired hard, does not.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.graph: Carbon comes in a form that marks paper and does not burn in a fire you can build.
advancement.feedback.progress.heat.lava_: Fire That Does Not Go Out
Some fires need no fuel and have no gap. Set a vessel where one burns.
advancement.feedback.progress.nether.arr: The ground itself is hot here, and there is no water. Go and see what a fire can do with it.
advancement.feedback.progress.ender.arri: Mail is not the same as being there. Go to where the port sends.
advancement.feedback.progress.ender.void: Nothing grows in the void, but something lives there. Dark and sealed works anywhere.
advancement.feedback.progress.deepdark.l: The deep dark answers to vibration. Set something to hear it, and keep what it heard.
advancement.feedback.progress.food.just_: Raw is no good and black is worse. Take it off at the moment between.
advancement.feedback.progress.food.dried: Water is what spoils food. Take enough of it away and the food outlasts the season.
key.feedback.suit_wheel: Suit ability wheel (hold, release over a segment)
screen.feedback.suit.node.head: Helmet
modular.feedback.role.servo.tip: A winding that drives the piece: the conductor sets how hard it pulls and how much of what it draws is lost as heat.
modular.feedback.role.gauge.tip: A lens over the suit's dials. Without one the suit tells you in words; with one, in figures, finer the clearer the glass.
modular.feedback.role.sensor_head.tip: A bundle of fibre that gives the helmet night sight and thermal sight; more fibre sees further.
modular.feedback.role.battery_bay.tip: A plate cradle in the chest that holds the battery the whole suit runs on.
modular.feedback.fig.suit_drive.tip: Amps the servo winding can carry: the piece's muscle. The suit draws a share of it for each ability.
modular.feedback.fig.suit_loss.tip: The share of what the servo draws that leaves as heat in the suit.
modular.feedback.fig.suit_gauge.tip: How finely the suit's dials read: lower is finer, from the clarity of the lens.
modular.feedback.fig.suit_sense.tip: Cells of fibre in the sensor head.
modular.feedback.fig.suit_bay.tip: Whether the piece holds the suit's battery.
feedback.jei.info.charging_gantry: A frame on an electrical line that charges the battery in the suit of whoever stands in it. Only the floor plate is solid: walk in. It asks for the battery's own charge current while the line is above the battery's volts, and a line over the battery's case wears the cells. Wire it like any sink.
feedback.jei.info.charger: A clip on an electrical line. Right click with one battery to put it in, empty-handed to take it out. A battery charges as a placed one does, wearing if the line is over its case.
feedback.jei.info.exosuit: A powered suit is ordinary modular armour with fittings added at the bench: a servo (a winding part of any conductor, on any piece), a gauge (a lens), a sensor head (fibre, on the helmet) and a battery bay (plate, on the chestplate) that holds the battery everything runs on. Wear the pieces, fit a charged battery in the bay from the suit screen (J), and hold V for the ability wheel: strength, jump and dash (hold B), plating, night sight and thermal sight. Servos make heat; past the limit the suit cuts out until it cools. Each piece also takes one upgrade module, a finished item of its own (see Suit Module): some tune the suit, and a few give the wheel a segment of its own: cloak, jet (hold G), shockwave, scan ping and EMP.
modular.feedback.role.upgrade.tip: A finished suit module, fitted whole. What it is and how strongly it works come from the module itself; it only works while the suit is powered.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.rebreather: A sealed mask with a scrubber: air lasts longer underwater. Sturdier material, longer breath.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.rangefinde: Extends your reach while switched on at the wheel.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.respirator: Filters the air you breathe: poison, nausea and hunger are cleared as they land, at a small draw.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.glare_filt: A shutter over the eyes: blindness and darkness are cleared as they land, at a small draw.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.long_lens: Extends thermal sight's range while switched on at the wheel.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.crash_line: A padded liner inside the helm: arrows, bolts and thrown things hurt less.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.reflex_lin: A wire from the visor to the servos: your arm swings faster. A better conductor links faster.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.heat_sink: Fins on the back: the suit sheds its heat faster. A better heat conductor sheds more.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.coolant_lo: Raises the heat the suit can stand, and fire it from the wheel to vent most of the suit's heat at once, which can bring the servos back after a cut-out.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.efficiency: A fat bus between battery and servos: everything the suit draws costs less charge. A better conductor wastes less.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.autodoc: A shot of repair on demand: fire it from the wheel to heal a good share of health at once, then it must cool before it fires again.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.reactive_p: Plates that push back: blows shove you less.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.blast_shel: A thick shell over the ribs: explosions hurt less.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.thorn_arra: Spikes in the plate: fire them from the wheel to hurt everything within arm's reach.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.thermal_li: A heated lining: the cold cannot freeze you while the suit is powered.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.magnet_pic: Draws nearby items to you while switched on at the wheel.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.fire_curta: A curtain of heat-spreading metal: fire hurts less. A better heat conductor protects more.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.strider_pi: Leg pistons that quicken your stride while switched on at the wheel.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.step_assis: Lifts you over a full block step while switched on at the wheel.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.swim_fins: Pumps and flaps on the legs: you move better through water.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.shock_abso: Hydraulic dampers in the thigh: falls hurt you less.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.grip_pads: Rough pads on the knee: soft ground, webs and water slow you less.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.load_frame: A frame down the legs takes the weight of a pack: it carries more before it slows you.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.stabiliser: Gyros in the hips: you sneak faster and are shoved a little less.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.mag_anchor: A heavy anchoring sole: blows shove you far less.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.heat_shiel: A heat-spreading sole and a cooling pump: standing in fire or lava will not burn you while the battery lasts, at a heavy draw.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.jump_coil: A coil under the heel: you jump higher. A better conductor kicks harder.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.landing_ge: Sprung feet: you can fall further before it hurts.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.rocket_spu: A hotter nozzle on the dash, and fire it from the wheel for a single burst of thrust along your look.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.stomp_actu: A piston in the heel: landing from a height shocks everything around you, at a draw per landing.
modular.feedback.desc.part.module_casing: The shell of a suit module. It carries the module's weight and keeps its core off the wearer.
modular.feedback.desc.part.module_wiring: The leads that feed a module's attachments. A heavier conductor wastes less of what the module draws and can feed more attachments.
modular.feedback.role.wiring.tip: The leads of a suit module. Its material must conduct: more current means more attachments fed and less of the draw lost as heat.
modular.feedback.fig.suit_wiring.tip: How well the module is wired: heavier conductors waste less of what it draws.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.cloak_fiel: A field of cold, quiet plate that bends the wearer's glow and shape away. Switch it on at the wheel; it draws all the while it holds.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.jet_pack: A thrust nozzle on the back. Switch it on at the wheel, then hold the jet key: it lifts, thinned by thin air, and burns charge fast.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.shock_ram: A ram in the heel that slams the ground when fired from the wheel: it knocks back and hurts everything near, then must cool before it fires again.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.scan_ping: A burst from the helmet that makes every living thing in a wide ring glow for a while. Fire it from the wheel.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.emp_coil: A coil that dumps a field into nearby creatures when fired from the wheel: they slow, weaken and lose the wearer, then must cool before it fires again.
feedback.jei.info.suit_module: A suit module is built at the bench from a casing (plate), wiring (wire) and one to four attachments and the support parts they need: some upgrades need a circuit as a controller, a battery as a power cell, or a motor, and a better one makes the upgrade stronger. Each attachment is a part of one kind (optic, filter, thermal, plating, actuator, thruster, coil), and the shape it is cut in is the upgrade it gives, so two attachments of one kind can do very different things. The material sets how strongly each works; heavier wiring feeds more attachments and wastes less. Fit the finished module into a suit piece; taking the piece apart gives the module back whole. It only works while the suit is powered. Drawing a suit module takes a treatise on robotics; building one takes its blueprint.
modular.feedback.desc.part.module_optic: Lens work: ranging, sight, filtering light and scanning. The shape it is cut in chooses which; its material must reflect light well to work hard. It is fed from the module's wiring.
modular.feedback.role.module_optic.tip: An attachment of one kind: a lens or sensor array. Each shape it is cut in is a different upgrade. The wiring can feed only a few attachments.
modular.feedback.desc.part.module_filter: Air handling for the wearer: rebreathing and scrubbing. The shape chooses which. It is fed from the module's wiring.
modular.feedback.role.module_filter.tip: An attachment of one kind: an intake filter. Each shape it is cut in is a different upgrade. The wiring can feed only a few attachments.
modular.feedback.desc.part.module_therma: Heat handling: sinks, loops, linings, shields and the cloak. The shape chooses which; its material must conduct heat. It is fed from the module's wiring.
modular.feedback.role.module_thermal.tip: An attachment of one kind: a heat exchanger. Each shape it is cut in is a different upgrade. The wiring can feed only a few attachments.
modular.feedback.desc.part.module_platin: Mounted plate and frame: reactive and blast plating, liners, thorns, anchors and frames. The shape chooses which; a harder, tougher material works harder. It is fed from the module's wiring.
modular.feedback.role.module_plating.tip: An attachment of one kind: an armoured insert. Each shape it is cut in is a different upgrade. The wiring can feed only a few attachments.
modular.feedback.desc.part.module_actuat: Joint and leg work: strides, steps, jumps, landings, grip, fins and the heel ram. The shape chooses which; a harder, tougher material works harder. It is fed from the module's wiring.
modular.feedback.role.module_actuator.ti: An attachment of one kind: a piston or joint. Each shape it is cut in is a different upgrade. The wiring can feed only a few attachments.
modular.feedback.desc.part.module_thrust: Burning thrust: a hotter dash and the jet pack. The shape chooses which. It is fed from the module's wiring.
modular.feedback.role.module_thruster.ti: An attachment of one kind: a thrust nozzle. Each shape it is cut in is a different upgrade. The wiring can feed only a few attachments.
modular.feedback.desc.part.module_coil: Electrical work: bus, repair, reflex link, magnet and EMP. The shape chooses which; a better conductor works harder. It is fed from the module's wiring.
modular.feedback.role.module_coil.tip: An attachment of one kind: a field coil. Each shape it is cut in is a different upgrade. The wiring can feed only a few attachments.
modular.feedback.role.controller.tip: A circuit the module is run by. Upgrades that need one work only with it, and a faster, quieter circuit makes them work harder. Read off the circuit itself.
modular.feedback.role.cell.tip: A battery the module carries for itself. Upgrades that need one work only with it, and a bigger cell makes them work harder.
modular.feedback.role.motor.tip: A motor or dynamo built into the module. Upgrades that need one work only with it, and a higher-rated one makes them work harder.
message.feedback.plan.measured: You measure it as you take it apart: the paper becomes a blueprint.
feedback.jei.info.blueprint_book: Holds blueprints like a bundle. Click a blueprint onto it to put it in, click it on an empty slot to take one out. A bench that wants a blueprint reads the blueprints in a book in its blueprint slot.
item.feedback.treatise_weapons_1: Weapons Treatise I: Blades and Heads
item.feedback.treatise_mechanical_1: Mechanical Treatise I: Engines and Flywheels
item.feedback.treatise_chemical_2: Chemical Treatise II: Heat and Compression
