tooltip.feedback.treatise: Hold it, in a binder or on a shelf against a Blueprint Table, to draw blueprints of the types below. Each volume is its own subject.
message.feedback.blueprint_table.no_trea: Drawing this takes %s: carry it, in a binder, or keep it on a shelf against the table.
message.feedback.treatise.written: Taking it apart, you write down what you learn: %s.
feedback.jei.info.treatise_binder: Holds treatises like a bundle; click a treatise onto it to put it in. The Blueprint Table counts the treatises inside as held.
feedback.jei.info.treatise_shelf: A shelf for treatises and binders. Put it against a Blueprint Table: what it holds counts as held by whoever draws there.
feedback.jei.info.blank_treatise: Take a machine, gun or powered-suit module apart at a bench with this in the blueprint slot and it becomes the volume of that school's treatise the item belongs to. A volume lets the Blueprint Table draw blueprints of the types it covers.
message.feedback.blueprint_table.cannot_: Put a blueprint in the left slot and blank paper in the right to copy it.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.anode_rod: A plain rod: the baseline current and the baseline life.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.anode_plat: A broad plate: 60% more current, but it lasts 56% less long.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.anode_bloc: A thick block: 20% less current, but it lasts about 2.4 times as long.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.core_bar: A straight bar: the baseline pull and the baseline reach.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.core_horse: Bent so both poles face the work: 40% more pull, 30% less reach.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.core_pot: Wrapped round the coil: 80% more pull, but half the reach.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.crank_shor: A short arm: 30% less lever, but it spins 40% faster.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.crank_stra: A plain arm: the baseline lever and the baseline speed.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.crank_long: A long arm: 40% more lever, but 25% slower.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.crank_offs: A jogged arm: 30% more lever for only 10% less speed.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.filament_c: A coiled wire: the baseline current and the baseline toughness.
A baked carbon thread: draws 40% more and burns out only at a 30% higher voltage.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.filament_f: A hair-thin wire: draws 40% less, and burns out at a 20% lower voltage.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.flywheel_s: Spokes to a rim: 40% less momentum, and the rim bursts at 20% fewer RPM.
A full disc: the baseline mass and the baseline rim strain.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.flywheel_r: A heavy rim on a web: 30% more momentum, but the rim bursts at 10% fewer RPM.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.impeller_c: Vanes flung outward: the baseline flow and the baseline lift.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.impeller_a: A propeller in the pipe: 60% more flow and 60% more load to turn, but half the lift.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.impeller_s: A screw in a barrel: 30% less flow and load, but 60% more lift.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.jar_flat: A flat sheet of glass: 30% less area, and half the leak.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.jar_lined: A foil-lined jar: the baseline area and the baseline leak.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.jar_rolled: Glass and foil rolled up tight: 50% more area, but 50% more leak.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.nozzle_rin: A ring of ports: the baseline burn and the baseline flame.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.nozzle_jet: A single hard jet: burns 50% more fuel, and the flame is 8% hotter.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.nozzle_wic: A wick fed by capillary: burns 40% less fuel, and the flame is 8% cooler.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.plate_fram: Plates stacked in a frame: moves twice the heat of plain tubes.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.rotor_scre: Meshed screws: 30% more flow, 40% less heating, 20% more load.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.rotor_sing: One rotor: the baseline flow, the baseline heating and the baseline load.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.rotor_twin: Two rotors in stages: 80% more flow, 20% less heating, 70% more load.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.shell_fire: Flame passes through tubes in the water: the baseline pressure rating, 20% less room for water.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.shell_flat: A flat box: holds only 35% of the pressure of a fire-tube shell, but has the most room.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.shell_wate: Water runs through tubes in the flame: 40% more rating than a fire-tube shell, 30% less room.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.store_slab: A low slab: leaks 30% more heat and holds 20% less of it.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.store_towe: A tall tower: leaks 30% less heat and holds 30% more of it.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.store_wall: A plain walled block: the baseline leak and the baseline mass.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.tank_box: A flat-sided box: holds only 35% of a cylinder's pressure, but has the most room.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.tank_capsu: A cylinder with domed ends: 40% more rating than a cylinder, but 12% less room.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.tank_cylin: A plain cylinder: the baseline pressure rating, with 20% less room than a box.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.tank_spher: A sphere carries load evenly: twice the rating of a cylinder, but only about half the room of a box.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.tubes_coil: Tubes wound into a coil: moves 30% more heat than plain tubes.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.tubes_finn: Fins along every tube: moves 60% more heat than plain tubes.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.tubes_plai: Bare straight tubes: the baseline heat moved.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.wheel_buck: Buckets that hold the water: 50% more power, but 30% slower.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.wheel_padd: Flat paddles in the stream: 30% less power, but 40% faster.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.wheel_slat: Slatted blades: the baseline power and the baseline speed.
modular.feedback.role.core.tip: The core the winding is wound on. Its material sets the core loss: the share of the power through it that turns to heat.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.cramped: While you crouch, your movement is %1$s%% of normal. Worn once however many pieces carry it.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.crown_lever: Knockback on you is %1$s%% of its strength while this is worn on the head. Worn once however many pieces carry it.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.leg_drag: Sprinting costs %1$s extra exhaustion a tick, and in water you move at %2$s%% of normal speed. Worn once however many pieces carry it.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.shaft_seal: Powder snow does not freeze you, but in water you move at %1$s%% of normal speed. Worn once however many pieces carry it.
modular.feedback.desc.trait.cushion_sole: Fall damage is %1$s%% of what it would be. Worn once however many pieces carry it.
modular.feedback.fig.pierce_resist.tip: Share of arrow and bolt damage the piece turns aside, from the plate's competence, its cover and how its shape meets a point. Worn pieces add by slot: chest most, boots least.
modular.feedback.fig.fire_conduct.tip: How readily the plate carries fire's heat in to the wearer: the material's thermal conductivity times the plate's volume. Metal conducts, cloth and leather do not. Burning or standing in lava, each worn piece heats and the wearer takes extra heat damage.
gui.feedback.blueprint_table.title: Title this blueprint
modular.feedback.axis.width.tip: How wide the part is across. A wider one covers more and hits with more of its face, and takes more stock and weighs more.
modular.feedback.axis.torso_length.tip: How far down the body the plate runs. Longer covers more and takes more stock.
modular.feedback.axis.face_opening.tip: How much of the face the helmet leaves open. Wider sees better and guards less.
modular.feedback.axis.crown.tip: How tall the helmet rises over the head. Taller takes more stock.
modular.feedback.axis.length.tip: How long the part runs. A longer one reaches or covers further, and takes more stock and weighs more.
modular.feedback.axis.shaft.tip: How high the boot rises up the leg. Higher covers more and takes more stock.
modular.feedback.axis.sole.tip: How thick the sole is under the foot. Thicker wears longer and takes more stock.
modular.feedback.axis.thickness.tip: How thick the part is. A thick one resists chipping and weighs more; a thin one bites deeper and is quicker.
modular.feedback.axis.head_size.tip: How big the head is. A big head weighs more, so it hits harder and swings slower; a small one is quick to swing and to throw.
modular.feedback.axis.edge_length.tip: How long the working edge, face or point is. A longer one takes more stock and weight for the work it spans.
modular.feedback.axis.face_size.tip: How big the shield's face is. A large face guards more and weighs more and slows you; a small one is quick and parries.
modular.feedback.axis.limb_length.tip: How long the bow's limbs are. Long limbs draw heavy and shoot fast but slow; short limbs draw quick and shoot light.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.curved: Like a sword blade, but forged with a bend along its length in a run of taps and heavy blows. It cuts on the draw and hits a little harder, and carries a dash.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.tapered: Like a sword blade, but drawn down to a point in a run of taps. Light, with its mass near the hand and the best reach for its length; it hits lightly and the fine edge chips. Quick thrusts build into a flurry.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.serrated: Like a sword blade, but with teeth ground along the edge in a run of heavy blows. It saws through the unarmoured and hits hard, but turns on armour.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.fullered: Like a sword blade, but with a groove ground down its length in taps and heavy blows. Lighter for its stiffness and a little quicker, with a slightly weaker edge.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.leaf: Like a sword blade, but swelling toward the tip in a run of taps. Its weight sits forward, so it hits well, and it sweeps a crowd with a flourish.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.heater: Like a shield face, but a flat top tapering to a point: five lengths of stock. Lighter than a round face of the same size.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.rectangula: Like a shield face, but a square-cornered slab: eight lengths of stock. Holds a fifth more, and the corners are weight to carry.
modular.feedback.desc.part.electric_gun_: The barrel of an electric gun: a conductor wound into a coil, laid as two rails, or shaped into an arc channel. Its conductor sets the current it carries before it wears.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.coil_barre: Two cells of stock wound into stages round the bore. Each stage adds energy; stages past what the barrel is long enough to fit are mostly wasted. The slug must be a magnetic metal.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.rail_barre: Three cells of stock laid as two rails. The slug bridges them and takes what the rails are rated for; any conductor will do. A longer pair keeps the push.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.plasma_bar: Two cells of stock shaped into an arc channel. A shot vaporises a conductor nugget into a short bolt that burns what it hits and falls off with distance.
modular.feedback.axis.stages.tip: How many windings the coil barrel has. Each adds energy, but only as many as the barrel is long enough for work well; more cost switching losses and heat.
modular.feedback.fig.shot_energy.tip: What a shot takes from the battery at full draw. A coil's is its stages; a rail's, what its conductor is rated for; a plasma bolt's, the arc.
message.feedback.electric_gun.too_big: This receiver takes a battery of at most %s cells.
tooltip.feedback.electric_gun.no_cell: No battery. Click the gun with one to load it.
feedback.jei.info.electric_gun: An electric gun. Load a battery by clicking the gun with it in your inventory, and take it out with an empty cursor; charge it at a Charger. Use fires, taking one metal nugget a shot and the energy from the battery. A coil barrel needs a magnetic metal and adds energy by stages, a rail barrel takes any conductor and what its rails are rated for, and a plasma barrel vaporises a conductor nugget into a short burning bolt. A weak battery gives a weaker shot. A battery over the receiver's voltage band shocks you and wears the receiver, wet air arcs to you, and a current over what the barrel carries wears it or fuses it. Each shot warms the gun, and a warm gun recovers more slowly.
modular.feedback.desc.part.spring_gun_ba: The tube a spring gun's pellet runs down. A longer barrel keeps the piston's push longer; a wider bore cuts a heavier pellet from each nugget and wastes more of the spring's energy.
modular.feedback.desc.part.spring_gun_re: The body a spring gun's barrel, piston and spring are fixed to. It is what the spring is rated against: a spring stronger than the receiver holds takes a set each time it is cocked.
modular.feedback.role.piston.tip: The small metal plunger the spring drives. It moves with the pellet, so a heavy piston takes a share of the spring's energy.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.air_standa: One cell of stock, an 8 mm bore: pellets of middling weight, a few dozen to a nugget.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.air_pellet: One cell of stock, a 5 mm bore: tiny pellets, many to a nugget, and little of the spring's energy is wasted. Each pellet hits lightly.
modular.feedback.desc.variant.air_slug: Two cells of stock, a 12 mm bore: a heavy slug, only a few to a nugget, that hits hard, but the wide bore wastes much of the spring's energy.
modular.feedback.axis.barrel_length.tip: How long the barrel is. A longer barrel keeps the piston's push going and shoots truer, and takes more stock.
modular.feedback.fig.spring_energy.tip: What the cocked spring stores: its volume times the stiffness of its metal.
modular.feedback.fig.air_efficiency.tip: The share of the spring's energy that reaches the pellet. A longer barrel keeps more; a wider bore wastes more.
modular.feedback.fig.draw.tip.air_gun: Ticks to cock the spring by hand, for a wielder of ordinary strength. A stiffer or bigger spring takes longer.
modular.feedback.fig.velocity.tip.air_gu: Muzzle speed of an iron pellet of this bore, against a vanilla bow's arrow.
modular.feedback.fig.joint.tip.air_gun: The spring's energy over what the receiver holds. Over 1 the spring takes a set each time it is cocked; far over, it snaps.
feedback.jei.info.spring_gun: A spring-piston air gun. Hold use to cock it by hand; use again to fire. It throws pellets cut from any metal nugget in your inventory: a bigger bore cuts a heavier pellet and fewer to a nugget, a denser metal hits harder. The spring's stored energy is its volume times its metal's stiffness; a longer barrel keeps more of it and a lighter piston wastes less. A spring stronger than the receiver is rated for takes a set each cocking, and far past it snaps and hurts you. The release is nearly silent.
